name: Anaqua Springs Ranch
metaTitle: Anaqua Springs Ranch, Boerne TX — Guide, HOA, and the ISD Surprise
metaDescription: Anaqua Springs Ranch: Boerne 78006 mailing address, BEXAR County land, and NORTHSIDE ISD — not Boerne ISD. Guard gate, dues, septic, and who it suits.
body:
Anaqua Springs Ranch is a guard-gated luxury acreage community off the Toutant Beauregard and Scenic Loop corridor, southwest of Boerne. Streets include Anaqua Springs, Anaqua Point, Caliza Bluff, Caliza Crest, Caliza Cove, Caliza Terrace, Carrizo, Cat Springs, Creekside Cove and Miranda Ridge. It is one of the highest-value communities in the Boerne search area, and it has a fact attached to it that most published descriptions get wrong.

## The school district — this is not Boerne ISD

**Anaqua Springs Ranch is in Northside ISD, not Boerne ISD.**

We verified this three ways:

1. **Bexar County's own school district GIS layer** returns **Northside ISD** for this location.
2. **Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder address lookup returns no assignment** for points inside the community. We probed nine separate parcels spread from the north end to the south end of the subdivision. Every one came back outside Boerne ISD.
3. The community's own website states Northside ISD.

This matters enormously. A buyer moving to the Boerne area specifically for Boerne ISD, who sees "Boerne, TX 78006" on a listing and assumes the schools follow, would be wrong — and would not find out until enrollment. Northside ISD is a fine district; it is simply a different one, with different campuses, different boundaries and a different calendar.

**Verify the specific campus assignment with Northside ISD directly.** We are not going to name campuses we have not confirmed for this address.

## The county fact

Anaqua Springs Ranch carries a **Boerne, TX 78006** mailing address and is in **Bexar County**, not Kendall County and not the City of Boerne.

The HOA's management certificate is captioned for **Bexar County** and was executed and notarized there (Bexar County Document No. 20220004772, filed January 7, 2022). Bexar County's parcel records carry all 220 parcels, with 151 of them showing a 78006 situs zip (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Consequence: Bexar County tax rates, Bexar County services, no City of Boerne taxes or services.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **220 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 1.69 acres** and a **median total appraised value near $1,507,000** (10th percentile around $960,000, 90th around $2,400,000). The median year built is **2013**, with construction running from 2005 through 2024.

The community's own materials describe **nearly 920 acres**, with lots averaging one to three acres and some estate lots up to five.

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices. Anaqua Springs is, by appraised value, the second most expensive community in this guide after Champee Springs Ranches — and unlike Champee, the value here is in the houses rather than the land.

## HOA — with the actual numbers

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Anaqua Springs Ranch Homeowners Association, Inc.**, managed by FirstService Residential San Antonio.

This is one of the few communities in this guide where the recurring costs are published. Per the community's own website:

- **Annual HOA dues: approximately $1,165 per year**
- **Gate Sentry fee: approximately $1,060 per year**, separate from dues, funding the 24-hour staffed gate

That second line is the one to note. Budget **both**. A staffed guard gate is expensive to run and it is billed separately here.

From the filed management certificate, the closing-table charges are a **$375 resale disclosure package fee** and a **$275 homeowner setup and unit transfer fee**, collected from the buyer at closing.

Because the dues figures come from the community's own site rather than a filed document, confirm both with FirstService Residential before your option period ends.

## Utilities — municipal water, private septic

An unusual combination, and the community documents it clearly:

- **Water: SAWS** (San Antonio Water System)
- **Electric: CPS Energy**
- **Internet, phone and cable: GVTC**
- **Sewer: private septic, homeowner-provided and maintained**

So you have full municipal water on a one-to-five acre lot, but every home is on its own on-site septic system. That is genuinely uncommon and it is worth understanding: you get reliable water without a well, but you own the wastewater problem. Get the septic permit, system type, and service history, and budget for an aerobic maintenance contract if that is what is installed.

## Amenities and gating

**24-hour guard-staffed gate** — not an automated keypad, an actual staffed entrance. Tree-lined private roads. A **five-acre community park** with a pavilion, a covered playground, a full-size basketball court, and walking and biking trails.

The developer is identified on the community's own site as Dreico Investments Inc.

## Location and commute

Off the Toutant Beauregard and Scenic Loop corridor. The community describes itself as roughly ten miles southwest of Boerne and about 26 miles north of downtown San Antonio. Practically, you are closer to the far northwest San Antonio amenities along I-10 than to downtown Boerne.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants an estate home on one to five acres with a manned gate, municipal water, and quick access to northwest San Antonio. It suits people who value security and privacy and are not buying for Boerne ISD.

It does not suit a family relocating specifically for Boerne ISD schools — this is Northside ISD, full stop. It does not suit a buyer who wants to be in the town of Boerne. And it does not suit anyone who budgeted HOA dues without adding the separate gate fee and the septic maintenance.

If you are considering Anaqua Springs Ranch and want the Northside ISD campus assignment confirmed in writing along with the real all-in annual cost, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

name: Balcones Creek
metaTitle: Balcones Creek, Boerne TX 78006 — Guide, HOA, Schools, County
metaDescription: Balcones Creek: a Boerne 78006 address that is legally in BEXAR County, not Kendall. 606 homes, Boerne ISD, Viola Wilson Elementary. HOA and taxes.
body:
Balcones Creek is a large master-planned community east of I-10 near Dietz Elkhorn Road, close to Fair Oaks Ranch. The street names are a mix of Hill Country wildlife and German settler surnames — Axis View, Bambi Place, Barefoot Way, Bearcat, Becker Crossing, Benedikt Path, Bettina, Catell — which is a fair description of the area's history in a single street index.

## The county fact — this is the important part

Balcones Creek has a **Boerne, Texas 78006** mailing address. 78006 is Boerne's own zip code. Nearly every listing you will read describes it as a Boerne community.

**Balcones Creek is in Bexar County.** It is not in Kendall County, and it is not in the City of Boerne.

Two independent sources confirm it. Bexar County's parcel records carry all 606 Balcones Creek parcels, with legal descriptions written against Bexar County Blocks — "CB 4707H (BALCONES CREEK UT-1A)" and similar — and 553 of those 606 parcels show a **78006** situs zip (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026). Separately, the community's HOA management certificate records the master covenant and every unit plat, Units 1 through 10 plus 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B and the Holman Acres Enclave, in the **Official Deed and Plat Records of Bexar County, Texas**.

Why this matters to you, concretely:

- **Your county tax rate is Bexar County's, not Kendall County's.** They are different. Model the actual bill.
- **You are not in the City of Boerne.** No Boerne city tax, no Boerne PD, no City of Boerne utilities.
- Permitting and county services run through Bexar County.

A zip code is a postal delivery route. It is not a county line, and in this corridor the two do not track each other. Any page that tells you Balcones Creek is in Kendall County because the mail says Boerne is wrong.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **606 parcels** in Balcones Creek, with a **median lot of about 0.195 acres** (10th percentile 0.15, 90th percentile roughly 0.35 acres) and a **median total appraised value near $633,000** (10th percentile around $470,000, 90th around $860,000). The median year built is **2017**, with construction running through 2024 (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Those are appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

A 2017 median build year makes this one of the newer established communities in the area — old enough to be finished and landscaped, new enough that major systems have not yet come due.

## Housing stock

Multi-builder production construction. Highland Homes, Perry Homes, Sitterle Homes, M/I Homes and CalAtlantic have all built phases here, across sections marketed as The Estates, The Gardens and The Preserves. Homes commonly run over 3,000 square feet, with four to five bedroom plans and three-car garages available.

New-construction phases are reported sold out, so this now trades as a resale market.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Balcones Creek Residential Community, Inc.**, managed by FirstService Residential from its San Antonio office on Huebner Road (TREC management certificate, Bexar County Document No. 20240157184, filed August 28, 2024). The master covenant was executed effective **March 21, 2013**.

Note that the same FirstService Residential office manages Napa Oaks and Fallbrook — so the management address tells you nothing about which community is which, and nothing about what county any of them is in.

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the management certificate. Texas only requires transfer-related fees on that filing. Get the current assessment from FirstService Residential directly before your option period ends.

## Amenities

Controlled access, a resort-style pool, a clubhouse, parks, and jogging trails. For a community of 606 homes this is a full amenity package, and it is a meaningful part of what the dues fund.

## Schools — Boerne ISD, and a recent change

**Balcones Creek is in Boerne ISD**, despite being in Bexar County. Bexar County's own school district GIS layer confirms Boerne ISD for this location, and Boerne ISD's InfoFinder address lookup returns **Viola Wilson Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** (both queried September 2026).

Pay attention to that elementary assignment. **Viola Wilson Elementary opened in August 2024**, and Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries when it did, moving roughly 469 students out of the Van Raub, Fabra and Kendall zones. Balcones Creek was affected. **Any listing or neighborhood page published before August 2024 that names this community's elementary school is likely out of date.** Verify your specific address with the district.

## Location and commute

East of I-10 near Dietz Elkhorn Road, adjacent to Fair Oaks Ranch. Interstate access is good, and the drive into San Antonio is short by the standards of anything with a Boerne address. Downtown Boerne itself is further — you are closer to San Antonio than to the Hill Country Mile.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants a large, newer home with a full amenity package, Boerne ISD schools, and a genuinely short commute into San Antonio. It suits families who will use a pool and trails.

It does not suit someone who wants to be in the town of Boerne — you are not, and the drive to downtown is real. It does not suit a buyer who wants acreage; lots are about a fifth of an acre. And it does not suit anyone underwriting a payment on Kendall County tax assumptions, because the county here is Bexar.

If you want current Balcones Creek listings, or a real tax-bill comparison against a Kendall County neighborhood at the same price, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

name: Bent Tree
metaTitle: Bent Tree, Boerne TX — Neighborhood Guide, HOA, Schools
metaDescription: Bent Tree, Boerne: 103 homes on roughly 1-acre lots north of town, unincorporated Kendall County. HOA, wells and septic, schools, commute.
body:
Bent Tree is a small acreage neighborhood north of Boerne with streets named for Hill Country plants — Anacacho, Madrone, Nolina, Spike Rush, Switchgrass — plus Bent Tree itself. It occupies a useful middle position that not many Kendall County neighborhoods do: roughly an acre per lot, which is enough for real separation without committing you to five acres of brush management.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **103 parcels covering roughly 142 acres**, with **94 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). At 91% built out, this is a finished neighborhood with only a handful of lots left.

Lot sizes are remarkably uniform: 10th percentile about **1.04 acres**, median **1.12 acres**, 90th percentile about **1.46 acres**. Almost everyone is on roughly one acre. That consistency is unusual and it makes comparables clean — appraisals here are predictable in a way they are not in neighborhoods with wide lot variation.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $948,000**, 10th percentile around $835,000, 90th around $1,128,000. A tight band. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

The appraisal roll shows three platted units — Bent Tree Unit 1, Unit 2 and Unit 3 — clustered north of town off the Curington Elementary side of Boerne. Homes are custom to semi-custom on acre lots, generally substantial, in the Hill Country vernacular.

We were not able to verify the original developer or a specific build era from a primary source. Pull the year built on the specific property from the appraisal record rather than relying on a listing description.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **The Property Owners Association at Bent Tree, Inc.** (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County).

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** on the management certificate — Texas only requires transfer-related fees on that filing. Contact the association directly for the current dues figure and for the recorded restrictions before your option period ends.

On a 103-lot neighborhood with private roads, ask specifically about road maintenance: who does it, how it is funded, and whether there is a reserve. Small associations frequently under-fund pavement and then face a special assessment.

## Utilities

Not verified from a primary source. On one-acre lots in unincorporated Kendall County, **individual wells and on-site septic are the expected arrangement**, though at this lot size a shared or community water system is also possible. Do not guess — confirm in writing for the specific property.

An acre is on the smaller side for a conventional septic drainfield, so pay particular attention to the septic permit, the system type, and whether there is room to replace the field if it fails. Get the permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Bent Tree parcels. **Unincorporated Kendall County** — no city property tax, no city services, county sheriff, rural fire response.

That is the central trade at Bent Tree: you are close enough to town that city services would be convenient, but you do not get them, and you do not pay for them either.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Curington Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries at the same time.

## Location and commute

North of Boerne, in the same general area as Durango Reserve and the Overlook. This is one of the closer-in acreage neighborhoods — the drive to downtown Boerne, to the H-E-B, and to Boerne High School is short by Kendall County standards. I-10 access is reasonable, though the San Antonio commute is still a commute.

For a buyer who wants an acre but does not want to spend their life driving, Bent Tree's position is its strongest feature.

## Amenities

We found no confirmed community amenities. This is a residential acreage neighborhood — the amenity is the lot size and the quiet.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants about an acre, a substantial house, and a short drive into Boerne, without the isolation of the five-acre communities further out. It suits people who want room for a shop or a pool but do not want to manage pasture. It suits someone who values predictable comparables and a stable, finished neighborhood.

It does not suit a buyer at the lower end of the market — the 10th percentile here is over $800,000. It does not suit someone who wants an amenity package or a gated entry with a guard. And it does not suit anyone who wants city water and sewer; on an acre in unincorporated Kendall County you should plan on a well and a septic system until proven otherwise.

name: Boerne Original Town / Boerne Historic District
metaTitle: Historic Downtown Boerne, TX — Original Town Guide, Rules, Schools
metaDescription: Boerne Original Town and the Historic District: no HOA, but Certificate of Appropriateness review applies. Lot sizes, values, schools, and real rules.
body:
This is the oldest part of Boerne — the platted town grid around Main Street, with streets named Blanco, Cibolo, Evergreen, Frederick, Hosack, Johns, Live Oak and Lohmann. It is the only part of the area where you can genuinely walk to a restaurant, and it is the only part governed by historic design review rather than by a homeowners association.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **114 parcels in the Boerne Original Town subdivision covering roughly 106 acres**, with **94 improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). Note that "Original Town" is a specific platted subdivision; the City's Historic District overlay is a separate boundary that covers a broader stretch of the Main Street corridor.

Lots vary enormously because this is a 19th-century town grid that has been divided and consolidated for 150 years: 10th percentile about **0.107 acres**, median **0.362 acres**, 90th percentile about **1.77 acres**.

Values vary just as widely — **median market value near $677,000**, but the 10th percentile is around $250,000 and the 90th around $2,415,000. That ten-fold spread is real. Original Town contains small cottages, substantial historic homes, and commercial buildings on the same tax roll. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices, and here more than anywhere else the appraised figure may diverge sharply from what a restored property actually trades for.

## The Historic District — what it actually requires

The City of Boerne established its **Historic District in 1985**. The district runs along Main Street between Frederick Street and Oak Park Drive, a little over a mile — the stretch marketed as the Hill Country Mile — and encompasses **over 150 properties** (City of Boerne).

**There is no HOA here.** That is genuinely good news for monthly cost. But it is not the same as no rules, and buyers who hear "no HOA" and relax are making a mistake.

The **Historic Landmark Commission** reviews permits for the "construction, reconstruction, alteration, restoration, relocation, demolition, or razing" of a structure in a designated historic district. That review results in a **Certificate of Appropriateness**, and you need one before the work proceeds.

Practical consequences:

- Exterior changes are a city approval process with a meeting calendar, not a weekend decision.
- Applications go through the City's SmartGov portal, and submittals are due to the Planning Department **a minimum of 14 days before the meeting date**.
- The Commission is a 7-member body appointed by the mayor with Council approval, serving four-year terms.
- To qualify for historic designation, a property generally must be **more than 50 years old**.

The City publishes Historic District Guidelines that spell out what specifically triggers review — paint, windows, fencing, signage, additions. **Read that document before you buy if you have any renovation plans at all.** We were not able to extract its detailed trigger list, and the City's own pages give inconsistent information about when the Commission meets, so call Planning at (830) 248-1501 and confirm both the guidelines and the meeting schedule rather than relying on a website.

The distinction that matters: an HOA is a private contract enforced by a board. Historic district review is a **city ordinance enforced by the City**. You cannot vote it away, and it runs with the property.

## Housing stock

The oldest housing stock in the county. Individually listed National Register properties within or adjacent to the district include the **Kendall County Courthouse** and the **Joseph Dienger Building** on North Main; the **Kendall Inn** on West Blanco is another landmark of the period. Residential stock runs from modest frame cottages to substantial two-story homes, with limestone construction reflecting the town's German settlement history.

We were not able to verify a specific architectural style inventory from the Texas Historical Commission or National Register nomination documents, so we are not going to characterize the prevailing styles beyond what the City itself documents. If period architecture is the reason you are buying, get the actual nomination paperwork for the specific property.

Expect the usual older-home realities: foundations that have moved, original wiring somewhere in the walls, plumbing of uncertain vintage, and possible lead paint and asbestos in pre-1978 construction. Budget for a specialist inspection, not a standard one.

## Jurisdiction

Kendall CAD shows the **City of Boerne** on every Original Town parcel. Obviously — this is the city. City utilities, Boerne PD, city trash, city tax.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point in Original Town returns **Curington Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). Confirm your specific address; boundaries were redrawn in August 2024.

## Location

This is the one place in Kendall County where "walkable" is a fair description. Restaurants, the Kendall County Courthouse square, shops, the library, and Cibolo Creek are all on foot. I-10 is a few minutes away.

The tradeoff is that you live in the part of town everyone else drives to. Event weekends, the Christmas lighting, Market Days, and Dickens on Main bring traffic and parked cars to your street. Some owners love it. Some list within two years.

## Who it suits

It suits someone who genuinely wants to walk to dinner, who values period character, and who is willing to work inside a design review process. It suits a buyer with the patience and budget to restore rather than renovate.

It does not suit someone who wants a garage, a big yard, a quiet street on a festival weekend, or the freedom to replace the windows next month without asking anyone. And it does not suit a buyer who hears "no HOA" and assumes that means no oversight — here, the oversight is the City, and it has more authority than an HOA would.

## Talk to someone who works this market

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you are considering a historic property and want help understanding what the Certificate of Appropriateness process will mean for your plans, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

name: Champee Springs Ranches
metaTitle: Champee Springs Ranches, Boerne TX — Guide, POA, Schools
metaDescription: Champee Springs Ranches, Boerne: 160 ranch tracts, median 38 acres, spanning Boerne ISD and Comfort ISD. POA status, easement litigation history, schools.
body:
Champee Springs Ranches is not a subdivision in any ordinary sense. It is a collection of working-ranch-scale tracts west of Boerne off Ranger Creek Road, reached from I-10, with road names like Busby Lane, Camino Cantera, Poste Robles, Turkey Knob, and Wild Turkey. You do not drive through it looking at houses. You drive through it looking at gates, cattle guards, and hills.

If you are searching for a neighborhood, this is not one. If you are searching for land with a house on it, this is the top of that market in Kendall County.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **160 parcels covering roughly 11,567 acres**, with **92 carrying an improvement** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). Note that acreage figure — this is by far the largest land area of any community in this guide, and it has fewer than 100 houses on it.

Tract sizes are the story: 10th percentile about **1 acre**, median **37.9 acres**, 90th percentile about **157 acres**. The median tract here is larger than the entire Woods of Boerne subdivision.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $2,064,000**, 10th percentile around $828,000, 90th around $4,573,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices. A large share of that value is land, not house — which matters enormously for financing, insurance, and property tax strategy.

## The agricultural and wildlife valuation question

On tracts this size, the single biggest carrying-cost variable is whether the land holds an **agricultural or wildlife management special valuation** with Kendall CAD. The difference between a tract appraised at market value and one under 1-d-1 open-space valuation is not small — it is frequently the difference between a manageable annual tax bill and an unmanageable one.

Before you write an offer on anything out here, confirm with Kendall CAD: does this parcel currently carry ag or wildlife valuation, what use qualifies it, and will your intended use maintain it? If the valuation lapses because you stop running livestock or stop executing a wildlife management plan, you can trigger a **rollback assessment** covering prior years plus interest. That is a genuine six-figure risk on a large tract and it is the most common expensive mistake buyers make on Hill Country acreage.

## Schools — this subdivision spans two districts

This is the fact that most published information about Champee Springs gets wrong.

Kendall CAD parcel records show **113 parcels in Boerne ISD and 47 parcels in Comfort ISD**. The subdivision **straddles the district line.**

For the Boerne ISD portion, a point inside the community returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). For the Comfort ISD portion, the assigned campuses are Comfort ISD's.

Do not accept a blanket "Boerne ISD" claim on a Champee Springs listing. Roughly 29% of the parcels are not. Verify the specific tract with both districts.

## POA status — genuinely unresolved, and you should know that

Here the honest answer is that we cannot give you a clean one.

**There is a property owners association.** The Champee Springs Ranches Property Owners Association appears by name as a named party in Texas appellate and Supreme Court litigation over access and easement rights across the original tract (*Teal Trading and Development, LP v. Champee Springs Ranches Property Owners Association*, decided by the Supreme Court of Texas in 2020). An association that litigates to the state's highest court is not a dormant one.

**But no current management certificate for it appears in the Texas Real Estate Commission's statewide HOA management certificate database.** Under Texas Property Code § 209.004, associations subject to Chapter 209 are required to file one. Its absence means either the association is not currently compliant with that filing requirement, files under a name indexed differently, or is structured in a way that falls outside Chapter 209.

At least one real estate marketing page states flatly that Champee Springs "does not have an HOA." **That claim is inconsistent with the litigation record and should not be relied on.**

What this means for you: **do not buy here on an assumption about the POA in either direction.** Get the recorded declaration and any amendments from title, read them, and ask the association directly what assessments exist. Also ask specifically about **road maintenance obligations** — on private ranch roads serving 37-acre tracts, road maintenance is often the real recurring cost and it is often handled by agreement rather than by a conventional HOA budget.

The easement litigation history is itself worth understanding before you buy. Ask title for a full easement and access review, not just a standard commitment read.

## Utilities

Individual wells and on-site septic, in all likelihood — there is no central utility infrastructure this far out. We could not confirm it from a primary source for specific tracts, so verify. On a tract this size, also confirm whether surface water rights, stock tanks, or spring features convey and what restrictions apply.

## Jurisdiction

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit**. Unincorporated Kendall County, with a portion of the original tract historically extending toward Kerr County. County sheriff, rural fire, county permitting.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants genuine ranch land with a house, who understands ag and wildlife valuation, and who has a lawyer and a title company look hard at easements and access before closing. It suits someone building a legacy property rather than buying a residence.

It does not suit anyone who wants neighbors, services, a short drive, or a clean, simple HOA answer. It does not suit a buyer who is not prepared to do real diligence — this is the one place in this guide where the paperwork genuinely matters more than the house.

## Talk to someone who works this market

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you are looking at a Champee Springs tract and want help pulling the ag valuation status, the easement history, and which school district it actually sits in before you commit, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

name: Champion Heights
metaTitle: Champion Heights, Boerne TX — Neighborhood Guide, HOA, Schools
metaDescription: Champion Heights, Boerne: 216 homes inside City of Boerne limits off Hwy 46. HOA, schools (it is zoned to Boerne High, not Champion), commute.
body:
Champion Heights is a mid-sized subdivision on the east side of Boerne off the Highway 46 corridor, with streets named Aspen, Champion, Destiny, Dovetail, Firefly, Gage, Vail and Parkview Terrace. It is an established, conventional neighborhood at a price point that keeps it in reach for a lot of buyers who want a Boerne address.

## The school-name trap — read this first

The neighborhood is called Champion Heights. It sits near Champion High School. **It is zoned to Boerne High School.**

A point inside the neighborhood returns **Dr. Ferdinand L. Herff Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder address lookup (queried September 2026).

This catches people. The subdivision name and the nearby campus both say Champion; the attendance zone does not. If you are buying here specifically so a student can attend Champion High School, **verify your exact address with Boerne ISD in writing before you go under contract** — and understand that a neighborhood name is marketing, not a zoning designation.

Boerne ISD also opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries at that time, so older listings and blog posts about this neighborhood's schools are unreliable.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **216 parcels across roughly 93 acres**, with **200 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). About 93% built out — a finished neighborhood.

The appraisal roll shows three platted units: Champion Heights Unit 1, Unit 2 and Unit 3.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.138 acres**, median **0.174 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.27 acres**. Conventional suburban lots, roughly a sixth of an acre.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $469,000**, 10th percentile around $381,000, 90th around $577,000. That places Champion Heights toward the affordable end of established in-town Boerne neighborhoods. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

Single-family production homes across three units built at different times, so expect some variation in age and style between sections. One and two-story plans, attached garages, conventional stone-and-stucco or stone-and-siding elevations.

We were not able to verify the original builder or specific square footage ranges from a primary source. Pull the year built and living area from the appraisal record for any specific property rather than relying on listing copy.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on all 216 parcels. This is inside the city limits: City of Boerne water and sewer, city trash, Boerne PD, and a city tax line on the bill.

On a sixth-acre lot that is the right arrangement. You are not maintaining a well or a septic field, and emergency response is city rather than rural.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Champion Heights Homeowners Association, Inc.** (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County).

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the management certificate — Texas only requires transfer-related fees on that filing — and we could not verify it from any primary source. Contact the association directly for the current assessment and a copy of the recorded restrictions before your option period ends.

Ask specifically what the dues cover. In neighborhoods inside city limits with public streets and no pool, dues are typically modest and fund little beyond common-area landscaping and covenant enforcement.

## Location and commute

East Boerne off the Highway 46 corridor. You are close to the Highway 46 retail, close to the H-E-B, and a short run to downtown Boerne and the Hill Country Mile. I-10 access for the San Antonio commute is reasonable.

This is a genuinely convenient location, and combined with the price band it is one of the better practical values inside the city limits.

## Amenities

We found no confirmed community pool or clubhouse. If an amenity package matters to you, Regent Park and Southglen both have pools at similar or slightly higher price points.

## Who it suits

It suits a first-time or move-up buyer who wants an established Boerne address inside the city limits, city utilities, and a short drive to everything, without paying for acreage or amenities. It suits commuters. It suits someone who wants a finished neighborhood with no construction traffic.

It does not suit a buyer who wants land, privacy, or a view. It does not suit someone who needs a community pool. And it very specifically does not suit a family buying for Champion High School on the assumption that the neighborhood's name guarantees the zoning — it does not.

name: Cordillera Ranch
metaTitle: Cordillera Ranch, Boerne TX — Neighborhood Guide, HOA, Schools
metaDescription: Cordillera Ranch in Boerne: 1,519 platted lots, 5,443 acres, unincorporated Kendall County. HOA, the seven clubs, schools, and who it actually suits.
body:
Cordillera Ranch is the largest residential development in Kendall County by a wide margin, and it does not feel like a subdivision. You enter off Highway 46 east of Boerne, and then you keep driving. Roads like Cordillera Trace, Bella Collina, Apple Rock, and Bluff Vista roll across ridgelines and drop into draws. Some stretches have no houses in sight at all. That is deliberate — the development was laid out so that a large share of the acreage stays undeveloped, and the result is that a 3-acre lot here often lives like a 10-acre lot somewhere else.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District's parcel records show **1,519 platted parcels inside Cordillera Ranch covering about 5,444 acres**, of which **981 currently carry an improvement** — meaning roughly two-thirds are built on and the balance are still vacant homesites (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). That vacancy rate matters: it tells you this is still an actively selling community, not a finished one. Kendall County Commissioners Court approved a further expansion of the development in June 2025.

Lot sizes run wide. The 10th percentile lot is about **1.05 acres**, the median is **2.95 acres**, and the 90th percentile is about **6.4 acres**. There are villa-scale lots in the Clubs Village sections and genuine ranch-estate tracts in the outer units.

On value: the current Kendall CAD appraisal roll shows a **median market value of roughly $1.52 million** for improved parcels, with the 10th percentile near $969,000 and the 90th near $2.72 million. Those are appraisal-district market values, not asking prices — a listing can sit well above or below its appraised figure. Use them as a sense of scale, not a price guide.

## Housing stock

Custom only. There is no production builder tract here. Homes are built to the POA's architectural guidelines, and the prevailing look is Hill Country — limestone and stucco, standing-seem metal or tile roofs, deep porches oriented at a view. Because build-out has run from the late 1990s to today, you will find 20-year-old homes on mature lots next to work that finished last year.

## HOA — and the club, which is a separate thing

This is the single most misunderstood fact about Cordillera Ranch, and getting it wrong will cost a buyer real money.

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Cordillera Ranch Property Owners Association, Inc.**, and unusually for a community this size it is self-managed rather than run by an outside management company. Its filed management certificate lists the association at 28 Cordillera Trace, Suite 2, Boerne, with a general manager on site (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County Instrument #366482, filed January 27, 2022).

That same certificate discloses the **closing-table charges**: a $300 resale certificate fee, a $300 transfer fee, and a **$2,000 working capital contribution**. Budget for that last one — it is larger than most buyers expect and it is due at closing.

**Recurring POA dues are not disclosed on the management certificate.** Texas only requires transfer-related fees on that filing, so the annual assessment number has to come from the POA directly. Do not rely on a figure you read on a listing site. Call the association.

**The Clubs of Cordillera Ranch are a separate organization with separate money.** Golf, tennis and swim, spa and athletic, social, equestrian, rod and gun, and the river club operate as a private club with its own initiation fees and ongoing dues, in tiers. Owning a home here does not automatically make you a member, and club dues are in addition to POA dues. Buyers routinely conflate the two and then discover the real monthly carrying cost after they are under contract. Ask for both numbers in writing before you waive your option period.

## Schools

Cordillera Ranch is in **Boerne ISD**. A point inside the community returns **Dr. Ferdinand L. Herff Elementary, Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder address lookup (queried September 2026).

Two cautions. Cordillera Ranch is large enough that units at opposite ends sit miles apart, and Boerne ISD explicitly warns that addresses near boundary lines must be confirmed with its Administrative Services department. The district also opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries at that time, so any school claim published before 2024 is suspect. Run your specific address through the district's lookup.

## Location and commute

The main gate is off Highway 46 east of town. Downtown Boerne is a manageable run for errands, but "manageable" depends heavily on which unit you are in — the 300-series units on the far side toward the Guadalupe add real minutes. To I-10 and then into San Antonio, you are looking at a genuine commute, not a hop. People who live here have generally decided that the drive is the price of the setting.

## Utilities — ask, because it varies by section

This is the second thing that surprises buyers. Utility service is **not uniform across Cordillera Ranch**. Some sections have central water and wastewater; much of the development relies on individual on-site septic systems, with central water available in some areas. That changes what you can build, where you can build it, and what your inspection needs to cover. Get the specific section's utility situation confirmed in writing rather than assuming what is true on one street is true on the next.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants acreage, privacy, and a view, who is genuinely going to use a private club, and who is at peace with driving. It suits someone building custom and willing to work inside architectural guidelines.

It does not suit a buyer who wants to walk to the Hill Country Mile, who needs a short commute into San Antonio, or who is stretching to make the purchase price work and has not yet counted POA dues, club dues, and a $2,000 working capital charge on top of the mortgage. It also does not suit someone who wants to close in 30 days on a turnkey house — the inventory skews custom and the good lots move through relationships.

body:
Coveney Ranch is a gated acreage community off Highway 46 east of Boerne, with streets named Coveney, Canyon Bluffs, Horizon Crest, Scenic Bluffs, Outlook, Reserve and Morning. The naming is not accidental — this is bluff-and-canyon country, and the lots that sit on the edges have genuine long views.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **91 parcels covering roughly 379 acres**, with **81 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). At 89% built out, this is a settled community with only a handful of vacant lots left.

Lot sizes are unusually consistent: 10th percentile about **3.02 acres**, median **3.47 acres**, 90th percentile about **5.14 acres**. Nearly everyone here is on three to five acres — there is very little variation, which makes values predictable.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $1,254,000**, 10th percentile around $923,000, 90th around $1,683,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices. Note that the 10th percentile is over $900,000; there is no inexpensive entry point at Coveney Ranch.

## Development timeline

The association's filed management certificate gives an unusually clear record: the **Declaration for Unit 1 was executed August 30, 1999**, **Unit 2A was annexed July 10, 2000**, and **Unit 2B was annexed September 17, 2001**. Secondary sources describe construction continuing to around 2011.

So the housing stock here spans roughly 2000 through 2011. Expect homes now 15 to 25 years old — a stage where roofs, HVAC systems, water heaters, and septic components are at or past their first replacement. On a house at this price point, that is a meaningful inspection and negotiation item, not a rounding error.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Coveney Ranch Homeowners Association, Inc.**, managed by Diamond Association Management and Consulting of San Antonio (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County by the County Clerk, filed February 8, 2024).

The filed certificate discloses only a **$175 transfer fee** — one of the lowest closing-table charges of any community in this guide.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate. Get it from Diamond Association Management directly. With a gated entrance and private roads across 379 acres, ask specifically whether the association has a funded road reserve; repaving is the expense that catches small acreage POAs.

One note for your title company: the certificate was notarized in Bexar County, which is simply where the management company's notary sits. The plats themselves — Units 1, 2A and 2B — are recorded in the **Deed and Plat Records of Kendall County**. The subdivision is unambiguously Kendall County.

## Utilities

Not verified from a primary source. On three-to-five-acre lots in unincorporated Kendall County, **individual wells and on-site septic systems are the expected arrangement**. Confirm it in writing for the specific property. Given the 2000-2011 build era, septic systems here are old enough that an inspection and pump-out should be non-negotiable, and aerobic systems require an ongoing maintenance contract — find out which type is installed.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit**. **Unincorporated Kendall County** — no city property tax, no city services, county sheriff, rural fire response.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Dr. Ferdinand L. Herff Elementary, Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in August 2024 when Viola Wilson Elementary opened.

## Location and commute

Off Highway 46 east of Boerne, in the same general corridor as Cordillera Ranch but considerably closer in. That is Coveney Ranch's practical advantage over the bigger acreage communities further out — you get three to five acres and a gate without the 25-minute drive to a grocery store.

The run to I-10 and then San Antonio is still a commute. Highway 46 east is a good road but it is not a fast one at 7:30 a.m.

## Amenities

We found no confirmed community amenities. This is a gated acreage subdivision, not an amenity community — you are buying land, views, and privacy, and the low transfer fee reflects an association that does not run much. If you want a pool, a clubhouse, or courts, look at Diamond Ridge or Cordillera Ranch instead.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants three to five acres with a view and a gate, reasonably close to Boerne, and who would rather pay for land than for amenities. It suits someone comfortable with an established home that will need work.

It does not suit a buyer who wants new construction, an amenity package, or an entry-level price. It does not suit a daily commuter into central San Antonio. And it does not suit anyone who skips well and septic diligence on a 20-year-old acreage home.

body:
Diamond Ridge is an acreage community southwest of Boerne with a gem theme running through every street sign — Blue Diamond, Brilliance, Crown Jewel, Gemstone, Heartstone, Marquise, Radiance, Regent, and Diamond Ridge itself. It is one of the more amenity-equipped acreage subdivisions in the county, which sets it apart from the plainer well-and-septic developments nearby.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **120 parcels covering roughly 847 acres**, with **86 currently improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). About 72% built out — there is still vacant land trading here.

Lot sizes: 10th percentile about **3.05 acres**, median **4.09 acres**, 90th percentile about **10.58 acres**. Four acres is the normal Diamond Ridge lot, with some substantially larger tracts.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $978,000**, 10th percentile around $750,000, 90th around $1,352,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Development era — sources disagree

The association's plat is recorded in Kendall County Map and Plat Records, Volume 4, Pages 264 through 271, and its management certificate was recorded May 24, 2022.

Secondary sources conflict on when the community was actually built out: one says it dates to 2004 with construction finishing around 2008, another says homes went up around 2011. **We could not resolve that from a primary source.** For a buyer it barely matters — what matters is the age of the specific house, which is on the appraisal record. Pull it.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Diamond Ridge Property Owners Association**, managed by Professional Community Management, an Associa company (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County, filed May 24, 2022).

The filed certificate discloses a detailed fee schedule: a **$45 new account fee**, a **$375 resale certificate**, a **$75 resale certificate update**, a **$220 legacy account closure fee**, and a **$75 refinance statement**.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed.** Get it from Professional Community Management directly, and ask specifically what portion funds the amenity park and the roads.

## Amenities — unusual for an acreage subdivision

Multiple sources describe a **private owners' park with a lake, a clubhouse, tennis courts, and a covered pavilion with a barbecue grill**. If accurate, that is a genuinely differentiated package — most acreage communities in Kendall County offer a gate and nothing else.

These descriptions come from real estate marketing pages rather than from the association, so verify what is actually built and open, and ask about the condition of the tennis courts and clubhouse specifically. Amenities at 120-lot communities can be under-funded simply because there are not many owners to spread costs across.

The community is consistently described as gated.

## Utilities

Not verified from a primary source. On four-acre lots in unincorporated Kendall County, **individual wells and on-site septic are the expected arrangement**. Confirm in writing for the specific property, and if it is a well, get the log, the depth, the pump age, and a water quality test. Get the septic permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Diamond Ridge parcels. **Unincorporated Kendall County** — no city property tax, no city services, county sheriff, rural fire response. Get an insurance quote early; rural fire ratings affect premiums.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). Confirm your specific address; boundaries were redrawn in August 2024.

Southwest of Boerne off the Highway 46 corridor. Closer in than Champee Springs or River Mountain Ranch, further out than the in-town subdivisions. The drive to the H-E-B and to Boerne High School is real but not punishing. I-10 and the San Antonio commute are a genuine haul.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants three to ten acres with a gate and actual shared amenities — a lake, a clubhouse, courts — rather than just a fence and a road. It suits families who want land but also want somewhere for kids to go that is not the backyard.

It does not suit a daily San Antonio commuter. It does not suit someone who wants new construction; most of this stock is 15 to 20 years old. metaDescription: Esperanza in Boerne: 1,608 platted lots, unincorporated Kendall County, WCID #3 utilities. HOA, the MUD question, schools, and who it suits.
body:
Esperanza is where most of Boerne's new-construction demand has gone. Drive north off Highway 46 onto Esperanza Boulevard and you are in a master-planned community with landscaped entries, a big amenity center, and street names like Amarosa, Bandalero, Cantina Sky, and Buena Vista. It reads as a complete place rather than a phase of one, which is unusual for something still actively building.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **1,608 platted parcels in Esperanza covering roughly 571 acres**, with **1,182 of them already carrying an improvement** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). Phases on the appraisal roll run from Phase 1 through Phase 4A, plus 2A, 2F, 2G, 2H, 3A, 3C, 3D and 3E — a lot of phases, which is what you would expect from a community marketed at roughly 1,700 acres at full build-out. The platted-and-appraised acreage above reflects what has actually been recorded so far, not the eventual footprint.

Lots are conventional suburban sizes: 10th percentile about **0.146 acres**, median **0.206 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.348 acres**. Builders market these as 50-, 60- and 80-foot lot widths.

The current Kendall CAD appraisal roll shows a **median market value near $599,000** for improved parcels, with the 10th percentile around $492,000 and the 90th around $791,000. Those are appraisal-district values, not list prices.

## Housing stock

New construction from national and regional builders — Perry Homes, Lennar, Toll Brothers, Coventry, Chesmar, Highland, Scott Felder and Drees have all been active here at various points. That means floor plans, design centers, and incentives rather than custom architects. The tradeoff is predictability: you know what you are getting, and you can usually get it in under a year.

Because the community has built continuously for years, "new" in Esperanza can mean a 2018 resale on a matured lot or a 2026 spec with bare landscaping. Those are very different products at similar price points.

## HOA and the tax question you must ask

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Esperanza Community Association, Inc.**, managed by Goodwin & Company (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County Instrument #354928, filed April 12, 2021). The association publishes CC&Rs by village at esperanzahoa.com, which is worth reading — the covenants vary between villages.

**Do not trust a dues number you find on a listing aggregator.** Published figures for Esperanza vary wildly across third-party sites, and Texas management certificates only disclose transfer-related fees, not the recurring assessment. Get the current assessment in writing from Goodwin & Company or the association before your option period expires.

**The bigger money question is the utility district.** Esperanza is served by **Water Control and Improvement District No. 3**, which the City of Boerne identifies by name in its own utility documentation as a customer of the City's wastewater collection system. A WCID is a taxing entity. That means an Esperanza tax bill can carry a district levy that a home inside Boerne's city limits with plain City utilities does not. Third-party sources put the combined effective rate meaningfully above 2.5%, but we have not verified the current district rate against the district's own filing, so treat that figure as unconfirmed and pull the actual rate before you underwrite a payment. This is the single most consequential line item on an Esperanza purchase and it is the one buyers most often miss.

## Jurisdiction — not inside Boerne city limits

Kendall CAD parcel records show **no city taxing unit** on Esperanza parcels. The community is in **unincorporated Kendall County**, not inside the City of Boerne. Practically: county sheriff rather than Boerne PD, county permitting rules, and no city property tax — offset, as above, by the utility district.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Dr. Ferdinand L. Herff Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). Herff Elementary sits adjacent to the community, which is a genuine daily-life advantage.

One caution worth taking seriously: Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries at the same time, moving roughly 469 students. Any school-zone claim published before 2024 may be stale, and Esperanza is large enough that future phases could be zoned differently. Confirm your specific address through the district.

## Location and commute

Esperanza's entrances feed onto Highway 46, and from there it is a short run into Boerne or out to I-10. The commute into San Antonio is real but ordinary by Hill Country standards — this is one of the closer-in master-planned options. Downtown Boerne and the Hill Country Mile are a drive, not a walk.

## Amenities

The amenity package is the draw: resort-style pool, lazy river, splash pad, fitness center, dog park, pickleball, and a trail network. The community markets more than 20 miles of trails and 450-plus acres of open space at completion. Whether a given amenity is open yet depends on the phase — verify what is actually built versus rendered, particularly if you are buying in a newer phase.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants a new house with a warranty, a full amenity package, a short drive to a top-rated elementary, and a Boerne address without a ranch-road commute. It suits families who will actually use a pool and a trail system.

It does not suit someone who wants acreage, privacy, or a mature tree canopy — lots are close together and much of the landscaping is young. It does not suit a buyer who wants the historic-Boerne character; this is suburban, and comfortable being so. And it does not suit anyone who has budgeted a payment without first confirming the WCID levy and the current HOA assessment.

body:
Estancia at Thunder Valley is a gated ranch community west of Boerne, off the highway and up into the hills. The street names are all variations on one theme — Thunder, Thunder Canyon, Thunder Creek, Thunder Hill, Thunder Valley, Thunder Verde, and Estancia itself. It is one of the least developed and most private communities in the county, and it is built around an amenity package that is genuinely unusual.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **87 parcels covering roughly 869 acres**, with only **36 currently improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). That is 41% built out — the lowest of any community in this guide. Most of Estancia is still land.

Tract sizes: 10th percentile about **3.0 acres**, median **7.06 acres**, 90th percentile about **17.3 acres**. Seven acres is the typical holding, and the largest tracts are substantial.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $1,606,000**, 10th percentile around $722,000, 90th around $2,674,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices. The spread reflects genuinely different properties — this is not a place where houses look like one another.

## Development

The association's filed management certificate records a **Master Declaration effective December 9, 2005**, an Amended and Restated Declaration effective May 19, 2010, and a further amendment in December 2019. So the community dates to the mid-2000s and has been slowly filling ever since.

That 20-year, 41%-built trajectory tells you something honest about the market for it: tracts here move slowly. That is a buyer's advantage on price and a seller's problem on timeline. If you buy, plan to hold.

## Amenities — the unusual part

Estancia's own materials describe an amenity set you will not find elsewhere in the county: an **equestrian center**, athletic and gym facilities, sport courts, a **par-3 golf hole or short course**, a **skeet deck**, trails, water features, and a resident **longhorn herd**. The community describes a gated entrance with an eight-foot security fence around the ranch.

These claims come from the community's own website rather than from an independent source. They are specific and plausible, but they are self-published. **Verify which amenities are actually built and currently operating before you buy on the strength of them** — amenity plans at slow-building communities have a way of remaining plans. Ask the POA what is funded and what is open.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Estancia at Thunder Valley Property Owners Association**, a Texas nonprofit corporation managed by Diamond Association Management and Consulting of San Antonio (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County Instrument, filed August 3, 2023).

The filed certificate discloses a **$175 property transfer fee** and a **$175 optional resale fee** — modest figures.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** and we could not verify it. This matters more here than in most communities: an equestrian center, a golf feature, a skeet range, private roads, and a livestock herd all cost money to run, and 36 improved lots is a small base to spread that across. **Ask for the current assessment, the budget, and the reserve position before you commit.** A community with expensive amenities and few paying owners is a setup for special assessments.

## Utilities

Not verified from a primary source. On three-to-seventeen-acre tracts in unincorporated Kendall County, wells and on-site septic are the expected arrangement, but confirm it in writing rather than assuming. Get the well log and water quality testing, and the septic permit history from Kendall County.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

## Schools

It does not suit a commuter, a buyer who wants neighbors and a finished community, or anyone who needs liquidity — with 87 tracts and a slow absorption rate, resale here takes time. name: Fair Oaks Ranch
metaTitle: Fair Oaks Ranch, TX — Guide to the Three-County City, HOA, Schools
metaDescription: Fair Oaks Ranch: an incorporated city spanning Bexar, Comal and Kendall counties. What county you buy in changes your tax bill and possibly your schools.
body:
Fair Oaks Ranch is not a subdivision. It is an **incorporated city**, and it is one of the few in Texas that sits in **three counties at once**. If you take away one thing from this page, take that.

## The three-county fact, and why it is the whole story

The Fair Oaks Ranch Homeowners' Association's own filed management certificate lists roughly 90 platted units, and it tags each one by county. The pattern:

- The large majority of units — the A, AA through AE, B-series, the C-related Fountains, Chartwell and Falls units, D, E, the FG series covering Front Gate, and H through T and V — are **Bexar County**.
- Units C-1 through C-15, the Enclave, and SF-1 through SF-4 are **Comal County**.
- Units K-1 through K-13 and the SCR units are **Kendall County**.

That is not a technicality. **The county your lot falls in determines your county tax rate, your county services, and potentially your school district.** Two houses on opposite sides of Fair Oaks Ranch can have materially different tax bills while sharing a mayor, a police department, and an HOA.

The city itself was **incorporated January 27, 1988**, with its charter recorded with the Secretary of State.

## The numbers

Because the city spans three appraisal districts, no single source gives a complete picture. What we verified:

**Kendall County portion** — Kendall CAD shows **622 parcels covering roughly 1,464 acres**, with **581 improved**, all carrying the **City of Fair Oaks Ranch** as a taxing unit and Boerne ISD as the school district. Lot sizes: 10th percentile about 0.56 acres, median **1.53 acres**, 90th percentile about 5.28 acres. Median market value on improved parcels: **roughly $795,000** (Kendall CAD GIS, retrieved September 2026).

**Bexar County portion** — Bexar County parcel records return **620 parcels** whose legal description includes "Fair Oaks Ranch," with a median lot of about **0.48 acres** and a median total appraised value near **$651,000**, built across roughly 1985 to 2024 (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026). That figure captures parcels whose legal description carries the name and is therefore a **partial count, not the city's total** — many Fair Oaks Ranch properties are described by block-and-lot without the name.

The pattern is clear even so: **the Kendall County side has larger lots and higher values; the Bexar side is denser and somewhat less expensive.** That is useful to know before you start touring.

The 2020 Census put the city's population at 9,833 across roughly 12.3 square miles.

## Housing stock

Everything from 1980s ranch-style homes on generous lots to current new construction in the newer units. Because the city has been building since the mid-1980s, housing stock varies by forty years. Golf-course-adjacent sections, wooded acre-plus lots, and denser newer subdivisions all coexist.

## HOA — the master association plus sub-associations

**The master association is mandatory**: **Fair Oaks Ranch Homeowners' Association, Inc. (FORHA)**, incorporated September 5, 1975, with its Fifth Amended Bylaws recorded in 2019. FORHA maintains the wildlife preserve and the walking and nature trail system.

**But FORHA is frequently not the only association you will belong to.** Many sub-neighborhoods inside the city have their own separate, separately-filed associations, each with its own dues and rules. Verified examples with their own state filings include:

- SA Front Gate Homeowners Association, Inc.
- Arbors of Fair Oaks Residential Community, Inc.
- Fair Oaks Gardens Homeowners Association, Inc.
- The Homeowners Association of The Fountains of Fair Oaks Ranch
- The Homeowners' Association of The Falls at Fair Oaks Ranch
- Trailside at Fair Oaks Ranch HOA
- Cibolo Trails Homeowners Association, Inc.
- Raintree Woods Homeowners Association, Inc.
- The Woods at Fair Oaks Homeowner's Association, Inc.
- Fair Oaks River Valley
- Property Owners Association of Stone Creek Ranch, Inc.
- Deer Meadow Estates Homeowners Association

**So the correct question is never "what are the Fair Oaks Ranch HOA dues."** It is: which associations does this specific address belong to, and what does each one charge? Two is common. Get both fee schedules in writing.

We could not verify FORHA's current dues amount from a primary source — the association's own site would not resolve and third-party HOA directories defer to the management company. Call FORHA directly.

Note also: the **golf and country club in Fair Oaks Ranch is a private club, separate from the HOA.** Membership is its own decision and its own cost.

## Utilities

The **City of Fair Oaks Ranch operates its own water and wastewater utility**, sourcing wholesale water from the Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority's Western Canyon transmission main supplemented by roughly 30 active groundwater wells. That is a genuine municipal utility, not a well and septic arrangement — a meaningful advantage over unincorporated acreage nearby.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD** serves the Bexar and Kendall portions. The city's own website names **Fair Oaks Ranch Elementary** and **Van Raub Elementary** as the two Boerne ISD elementary campuses within city limits.

Our verification: points in both the Bexar and Kendall portions return **Fair Oaks Ranch Elementary, Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). Bexar County's school district GIS layer independently confirms **Boerne ISD** for the Bexar portion.

**The Comal County portion is the open question.** Secondary sources indicate the Comal-side units may be zoned to **Comal ISD** — Rahe Bulverde Elementary, Spring Branch Middle, Smithson Valley High. We were not able to verify that against a Comal ISD boundary source and we are not going to assert it. If you are buying in Units C-1 through C-15, the Enclave, or SF-1 through SF-4, **verify the school assignment with both districts in writing.** This is the highest-stakes unresolved fact in this guide.

## Location and commute

Fair Oaks Ranch sits along I-10 between San Antonio and Boerne, with access from Ralph Fair Road, Fair Oaks Parkway, Old Fredericksburg Road, and Boerne Stage Road. The commute into San Antonio is among the best of any community in this guide — this is the closest-in option with a Boerne-area character.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants a city government, a municipal water utility, mature trees and generous lots, a genuine golf community, and the shortest commute in the area. It suits people who want established rather than new.

It does not suit a buyer who wants a simple, single HOA and a single tax jurisdiction — Fair Oaks Ranch is administratively complex by design. It does not suit someone who wants the historic Boerne downtown experience; this is a separate city. And it absolutely does not suit a buyer who writes an offer without first establishing which county the lot is in.

## Talk to someone who works this market

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you are looking in Fair Oaks Ranch and want the county, the full list of associations, both fee schedules, and a written school confirmation for a specific address, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

Call or text **[830-446-3847](tel:+1-830-446-3847)** · Email **[heath.shepard@kw.com](mailto:heath.shepard@kw.com)**

body:
Fallbrook is a gated subdivision off I-10 near Ralph Fair Road, on the Old Fredericksburg Road side between Fair Oaks Parkway and Ralph Fair. Streets include Anemone Bend and Narcissus Path — the plant-name convention that marks a lot of 2010s development in this corridor.

## County and jurisdiction

**Fallbrook is in Bexar County.** The SA Fallbrook Property Owners Association's management certificate lists every subdivision plat — Units 1, 1A, 1B, 1C, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7A — as recorded in the **Official Deed and Plat Records of Bexar County, Texas**. Bexar County parcel records carry all 415 parcels.

The mailing address is **Boerne, TX 78015**, which is a postal designation. This is **not** the City of Boerne and **not** Kendall County. Bexar County tax rates apply.

We could not confirm from a primary source whether Fallbrook sits in unincorporated Bexar County or inside a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction. No source claims it is inside any incorporated city.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **415 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 0.186 acres** (10th percentile 0.15, 90th percentile roughly 0.30 acres) and a **median total appraised value near $583,000** (10th percentile around $455,000, 90th around $800,000). Construction runs from roughly 2014 through 2024 (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

Production single-family homes. The original Declaration of Covenants for Fallbrook was executed **September 6, 2013**, with Unit 2 annexed in October 2014 — so this is a 2013-onward community, one of the newer ones in the corridor. **D.R. Horton** has been the primary builder in recent phases.

Reported square footages run roughly **2,006 to 3,795 square feet**. Individual resale lots run about 0.19 to 0.23 acres, consistent with the parcel data.

A 2014-2024 build window means most homes here are still in their first decade. Systems are young. That is a real advantage over the older 78015 inventory.

## HOA — the dues figures in circulation do not agree

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **SA Fallbrook Property Owners Association**, managed by FirstService Residential from its San Antonio office on Huebner Road — the same office that manages Balcones Creek and Napa Oaks.

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the management certificate, and here the secondary sources are genuinely contradictory. Individual listings have cited **$416 semi-annually**, **$69 monthly**, and **$600 annually** for different properties in the same community. Those cannot all be the current community-wide assessment.

**Do not use any of those numbers.** Get the actual current fee schedule from FirstService Residential in writing. This is a good example of why a dues figure copied from a listing site is worth nothing.

## Amenities and gating

**Neighborhood swimming pool, park, playground and clubhouse.** The community is described as gated across multiple sources; we could not confirm whether the gates are staffed or automated.

For a community of this size and price point, that is a solid, standard amenity package.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** Bexar County's own school district GIS layer returns Boerne ISD for this location, and Boerne ISD's InfoFinder address lookup returns **Van Raub Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** (both queried September 2026).

Verify your specific address with the district. Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries then, with Van Raub among the campuses affected. Fallbrook sits close to the boundary between the Van Raub and Fair Oaks Ranch Elementary zones — nearby Lost Creek, a mile or so away, is not even in Boerne ISD. Boundaries in this corridor are tight and consequential.

## Utilities

Not independently confirmed. Confirm the water and wastewater provider in writing for the specific property before closing.

## Location and commute

Off I-10 near Ralph Fair Road, roughly at Exit 550. Interstate access is immediate. This is one of the strongest commuter positions in this guide for anyone working in northwest San Antonio or downtown.

Downtown Boerne is a genuine drive from here — fifteen minutes or so up I-10 — so if the draw for you is the Hill Country Mile and the historic town, understand that you will be driving to it, not living in it.

## Who it suits

It suits a commuter who wants a newer home, a gated neighborhood with a pool and a clubhouse, and Boerne ISD schools, with immediate I-10 access. It suits families who want a low-maintenance house with young systems.

It does not suit a buyer who wants acreage, privacy, or the Hill Country setting. It does not suit someone who wants to be in the town of Boerne. And it does not suit anyone who underwrites a payment using a dues figure pulled off a listing page — in this neighborhood especially, those numbers are all over the map.
