body:
Front Gate is a gated master-planned neighborhood inside the Fair Oaks Ranch area, a few miles off I-10 outside Loop 1604. It is one of the more active new-construction communities in the corridor, and the address on a Front Gate listing will usually read Boerne or Fair Oaks Ranch, 78015.

## County and jurisdiction

**Front Gate is in Bexar County.** The SA Front Gate Homeowners Association's amended management certificate lists every subdivision plat — Units 2B, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 and their amendments — as recorded in the **Official Public Records of Bexar County, Texas** (Bexar County Document No. 20250138509, filed July 29, 2025). Bexar County parcel records carry all 478 parcels.

The Fair Oaks Ranch master association's own certificate separately lists a series of "FG" units among its **Bexar County** platted units, which ties Front Gate administratively to the larger Fair Oaks Ranch community.

**What we could not confirm:** whether Front Gate sits inside the **City of Fair Oaks Ranch** corporate limits or in its extraterritorial jurisdiction. That distinction affects city services, city taxes and permitting. Ask the City of Fair Oaks Ranch directly for the specific address — it is a five-minute phone call and it changes your tax bill.

What is certain: this is **not** the City of Boerne, and it is **not** Kendall County, regardless of the mailing address.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **478 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 0.21 acres** (10th percentile 0.16, 90th percentile roughly 0.35 acres) and a **median total appraised value near $595,000** (10th percentile around $450,000, 90th around $815,000). Construction runs from roughly 2014 through 2024 (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

The earliest plat on the association's certificate — Unit 3 — was recorded in 2013, with later units recorded through 2022. So this is a community that has been building steadily for a decade and is still going.

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

Production new construction from several builders, including **Highland Homes, Ashton Woods and Gehan Homes**. Expect current-generation plans, design-center finishes, builder warranties, and the usual range from single-story three-bedroom plans up through larger two-story homes.

Lots were laid out to preserve mature oaks in places, and the community markets greenbelt frontage on some sections. Lot premiums for trees and greenbelt are real here — decide whether you are paying for something you will actually enjoy.

## HOA — check for two

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **SA Front Gate Homeowners Association, Inc.**

One secondary source reports dues around **$600 per year**. That figure is not confirmed against the association's own schedule and we would not rely on it.

More importantly: because Front Gate's plats appear within the Fair Oaks Ranch master association's unit list, **you may owe assessments to two associations** — the Front Gate sub-association and the Fair Oaks Ranch master association (FORHA). That is a common structure in this corridor and it is a common budgeting surprise.

**Ask explicitly: which associations will I be a member of, and what does each one charge?** Get both fee schedules in writing before your option period ends.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** Bexar County's own school district GIS layer returns Boerne ISD for this location, and Boerne ISD's InfoFinder address lookup returns **Van Raub Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** (both queried September 2026).

Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries at that time — Van Raub was one of the campuses that received enrollment relief. Front Gate remains zoned to Van Raub per our lookup, but given the recency of the change, verify your specific address with the district.

Some builder marketing references an elementary school within the community. Confirm what that refers to and whether your address is actually zoned to it.

## Utilities

Not independently confirmed. Given the location within the Fair Oaks Ranch area, City of Fair Oaks Ranch water and wastewater service is plausible — that city operates its own utility, drawing wholesale water from the Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority plus groundwater wells. **But we did not verify it for Front Gate specifically,** and it depends on the city-limits question above. Confirm the actual water and wastewater provider in writing.

## Gating

Described consistently as gated. We could not confirm whether the gates are staffed or automated. If that matters — and for many buyers it does — look at it on a tour.

## Location and commute

A few miles off I-10 outside Loop 1604. This is one of the shortest commutes into San Antonio of any community in this guide. Downtown Boerne, by contrast, is a real drive — you are in the Boerne postal area, not the town.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants new construction with a builder warranty, Boerne ISD schools, a gated neighborhood, and the shortest practical drive into San Antonio. It suits commuters who want the Boerne school district without the Boerne drive.

It does not suit a buyer who wants acreage or the Hill Country experience — this is suburban and close-set. It does not suit someone who wants to walk to downtown Boerne. And it does not suit anyone who has budgeted for one HOA without checking whether there are two.

name: Highlands Ranch
metaTitle: Highlands Ranch, Boerne TX 78006 — Guide, HOA, Schools, County
metaDescription: Highlands Ranch, Boerne 78006: acreage estates off Boerne Stage Road that are legally in BEXAR County. Boerne ISD, Viola Wilson. HOA and diligence.
body:
Highlands Ranch is a gated acreage community off Boerne Stage Road, southeast of Boerne proper. It is small — 111 parcels — and the lots are large, which puts it in a different category from the tract subdivisions that dominate this part of the corridor.

## The county is in the HOA's legal name

This is the cleanest county confirmation in this entire guide, because the association put the answer in its own corporate name.

The association is legally called **"Bexar County Highlands Ranch Homeowners Association, Inc."**

That is not a typo and it is not a clerical quirk. The subdivision plats — Units 1 through 6 — are recorded in the **Deed and Plat Records of Bexar County**, and the association's management certificate was recorded with the Bexar County Clerk (Document No. 20260036472, filed February 27, 2026). Bexar County's parcel records carry all 111 parcels.

The mailing address is **Boerne, TX 78006** — the same zip as downtown Boerne. **The land is in Bexar County.** Bexar County tax rates, Bexar County services, no City of Boerne anything.

A second naming caution: there is a large, well-known **Highlands Ranch in Douglas County, Colorado**, in the Denver metro. It dominates generic web searches for the name. Nothing you read about that place applies here.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **111 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 3.56 acres** (10th percentile roughly 1.5 acres, 90th percentile roughly 6 acres) and a **median total appraised value near $1,062,000** (10th percentile around $700,000, 90th around $1,600,000). Construction runs from roughly 1999 through 2022 (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

The build window is the thing to notice. **This community started around 1999 and filled in slowly over two decades.** That means the housing stock spans 25 years, and the oldest homes here are a full generation older than the newest. A 1999 house and a 2022 house on adjacent three-acre lots are completely different purchases. Pull the year built on the specific property.

## Housing stock

Custom homes on acreage, built to architectural guidelines. Descriptions of the community reference limestone exteriors and cedar shutters — the late-1990s and 2000s Hill Country idiom. Weston Dean Custom Homes has been active here.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Bexar County Highlands Ranch Homeowners Association, Inc.**, managed by Diamond Association Management and Consulting of San Antonio.

The filed certificate discloses a **$175 transfer fee** and a **$175 optional resale fee** — among the lowest closing-table charges of any community in this guide.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate. Get it from Diamond Association Management directly. On a gated community with private roads serving 111 large lots, ask specifically whether the association has a funded road reserve — with that few owners spreading pavement costs, it is a fair question.

## Utilities — ask, and plan for septic

We could not verify water and wastewater service from a primary source.

Look at the nearest comparable: **Anaqua Springs Ranch**, a few miles away in the same Bexar County corridor, has **SAWS municipal water but private homeowner-maintained septic** on every lot. That combination is common in this area — municipal water reaches out along the corridor, centralized sewer does not.

**Do not assume either way for Highlands Ranch.** Confirm the actual water provider and the wastewater arrangement in writing. If it is septic — likely on three-and-a-half-acre lots — get the permit, the system type, and the service history, and note that systems installed in 1999 through the mid-2000s are now at or past typical service life.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** Bexar County's own school district GIS layer returns Boerne ISD for this location, and Boerne ISD's InfoFinder address lookup returns **Viola Wilson Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** (both queried September 2026).

That elementary assignment is recent. **Viola Wilson Elementary opened in August 2024** on Corley Road, and Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries when it did. Any description of this community's schools written before then is likely wrong.

There is also a sharper local caution. **Anaqua Springs Ranch and Sundance Ranch, both nearby off Toutant Beauregard and Scenic Loop, are in Northside ISD — not Boerne ISD.** The Boerne ISD boundary runs through this area unevenly. Being on the Boerne ISD side is a real feature of Highlands Ranch, and it is not something you should assume applies to a neighboring subdivision, or that a neighboring subdivision's status applies here. Verify the exact address.

## Location and commute

Off Boerne Stage Road, southeast of Boerne. You are between Boerne and northwest San Antonio, with reasonable access to I-10. The San Antonio commute is moderate and the drive into downtown Boerne is a genuine trip.

This is a quieter, more wooded corridor than the I-10 frontage subdivisions, and the acreage keeps neighbors at a distance.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants three to six acres, a gated entrance, a custom home, and **Boerne ISD schools while living in Bexar County**. That last combination is genuinely hard to find and it is the main reason to look here.

It does not suit a buyer who wants new construction — most of this stock is 15 to 25 years old. It does not suit someone who wants amenities; there are none confirmed. And it does not suit anyone who skips well, septic, and utility diligence on an acreage property of this vintage.

## Talk to someone who works this market

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you want current Highlands Ranch listings, or help confirming the utility arrangement and school zoning for a specific address, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

name: Indian Springs (Kendall County)
metaTitle: Indian Springs (Kendall County), Boerne TX — Guide, POA, Schools
metaDescription: Indian Springs in Kendall County, Boerne: 22 acreage tracts off Hwy 46, volunteer-run POA with zero transfer fees. Not the Bexar County Indian Springs.
body:
Indian Springs is a very small acreage community west of Boerne off Highway 46, reached from Indian Springs Trail and Chinkapin Pass. With 22 parcels it is the smallest community covered in this guide, and it has one genuinely remarkable feature that we will get to.

## First: there are several Indian Springs, and only one is this one

This is the most name-collided community in the Boerne area. There are **at least four separate "Indian Springs" homeowners associations registered in Bexar County**, clustered around the US-281 corridor in San Antonio 78258:

- Indian Springs Property Owners Association, Inc.
- Indian Springs Residential Community, Inc. (covering The Preserve at Indian Springs)
- Indian Springs (Bexar Co.) Property Owners Association, Inc.
- Indian Springs Estates Homeowners Association

The Kendall County community is a different place entirely, and its association knows it — the association's own legal name is literally **"Indian Springs Property Owners Association – Kendall County, Texas."** They put the county in the corporate name specifically to avoid this confusion.

Practical consequence: **almost any general web search result about "Indian Springs" near San Antonio is about a Bexar County community, not this one.** Claims you may encounter about a founding date in 1988, a Hillwood development history, a location twenty miles up US 281, a community pool and cabana, or a gated entrance all appear to belong to one of the Bexar County associations. Do not carry them over. We could not verify any of them for the Kendall County community.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **22 parcels covering roughly 104 acres**, with **14 improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). Eight tracts remain unbuilt.

Lot sizes: 10th percentile about **3.15 acres**, median **3.96 acres**, 90th percentile about **5.16 acres**. Four acres is typical.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $661,000**, 10th percentile around $545,000, 90th around $1,042,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

At roughly four acres for a median in the $600,000s, this is among the better land-per-dollar positions in Kendall County — a function of scale, of being an older and plainer community, and of having no amenities to fund.

## The POA — and the zero-dollar fee schedule

**There is a mandatory association**, and it is unlike any other in this guide.

The **Indian Springs Property Owners Association – Kendall County, Texas** is **self-managed by volunteers** — no management company, no professional agent. Its CC&Rs and bylaws are recorded in Kendall County records, and the filed management certificate was acknowledged before a notary in Kendall County.

The remarkable part: the certificate lists a **resale certificate fee of $0.00, a transfer fee of $0.00, and a working capital charge of $0.00.**

Every other association in this guide charges somewhere between $175 and $2,000 at closing. This one charges nothing. That is not an oversight in our research — it is what the filed certificate says.

**The recurring annual assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate, and with a volunteer board there is no management company to call. The certificate names a treasurer as the designated representative; contact the association directly through the information on that filing to learn what, if anything, owners pay annually.

A word of realism: a 22-lot volunteer association with no fees has very limited capacity. That means low cost and light-touch governance, and it also means limited ability to maintain shared infrastructure or enforce covenants. Ask specifically who maintains the roads and how that is paid for.

## Utilities

Not verified from a primary source. On four-acre lots in unincorporated Kendall County, **individual wells and on-site septic are the expected arrangement.** Confirm in writing for the specific property, and get the well log, depth, pump age, and water quality testing, plus the septic permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Indian Springs parcels. **Unincorporated Kendall County** — no city property tax, no city services, county sheriff, rural fire response.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). Confirm your specific address; boundaries were redrawn in August 2024.

## Location and commute

Kendall Creek Estates is a small neighborhood on the south side of Boerne near Scenic Loop Road, with streets named Deerwood Oaks, Katie, Sage Canyon, Shadow Knolls, Sutter Mills and Winding. At 102 homes it is the kind of place where the same cars are in the same driveways every evening.

body:
Kendall Pointe is a one-acre-lot neighborhood on the south side of Boerne, with a short, simple street list: Kendall Pointe, Kendall Ridge, Kendall, and Canyon. It is close to I-10, which makes it one of the more commuter-friendly acreage-adjacent neighborhoods in Kendall County.

## The county question

Kendall Pointe carries a **Boerne, TX 78015** mailing address, and most 78015 properties around here are in **Bexar County**. Kendall Pointe is not.

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **Kendall County** on all 112 Kendall Pointe parcels, with **no city taxing unit** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). So: Kendall County, unincorporated, outside the City of Boerne.

That combination — Kendall County but not in the city — means you get Kendall County tax rates and Boerne ISD schools without a city property tax line, and correspondingly without city police, city trash, or city utilities.

## The numbers

Kendall CAD records show **112 parcels covering roughly 111 acres**, with **109 already improved** (retrieved September 2026). At 97% built out this is a finished neighborhood.

Lot sizes are tightly clustered: 10th percentile about **0.65 acres**, median **1.0 acres**, 90th percentile about **1.19 acres**. Essentially everyone is on an acre.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $727,000**, 10th percentile around $607,000, 90th around $932,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

For a buyer who wants a full acre with Boerne ISD schools and good interstate access, this is one of the more efficient ways to get it — you are paying less than Bent Tree or Coveney Ranch for comparable or slightly smaller land, with a better commute.

## Housing stock

Single-family homes on acre lots. The uniformity of lot size and the tight value band point to a coordinated development rather than a piecemeal one.

We were not able to verify the builder, build era, or square footage ranges from a primary source. Pull the year built and living area from the appraisal record for any specific property.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Kendall Pointe Homeowners Association** (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County).

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** on the management certificate. Contact the association directly for current dues and the recorded restrictions before your option period ends.

Ask specifically about road maintenance. In unincorporated Kendall County, neighborhood roads are either county-maintained or private — and if they are private, the HOA carries the repaving obligation for 112 homes. Find out which it is and whether a reserve exists.

## Utilities — likely well and septic

Not verified from a primary source. On one-acre lots in unincorporated Kendall County, **individual wells and on-site septic systems are the expected arrangement.** Confirm in writing for the specific property.

One acre is workable but not generous for a conventional septic drainfield, so look carefully at the septic permit, the system type — conventional or aerobic — and whether there is space to replace the field if it fails. Aerobic systems require an ongoing maintenance contract, which is a recurring cost most buyers do not price in. Get the permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program.

If it is a well: log, depth, pump age, pressure tank, and both bacteriological and mineral water testing.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Kendall Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries then, and neighborhoods in this part of the district were directly affected — nearby Kendall Creek Estates now feeds Wilson rather than Kendall Elementary.

## Location and commute

South Boerne, close to I-10. This is the practical argument for Kendall Pointe: an acre of land and a short drive to the interstate is a rare combination around here. The San Antonio commute from this position is about as good as acreage living gets in Kendall County.

Downtown Boerne and the Highway 46 corridor are short drives. The H-E-B is easy.

## Amenities

We found no confirmed community amenities. This is a residential acreage neighborhood — you are buying the lot size and the location.

## Who it suits

It suits a commuter who wants an acre, Boerne ISD schools, and no city tax, and who is comfortable with a well and a septic system. It suits someone who wants land but cannot afford the drive time that usually comes with it. It suits buyers who want a finished neighborhood with predictable values.

Kendall Woods Estates is an established acreage subdivision east of Boerne off FM 3351, with streets named Kendall Woods, Kendall View, Forest Ridge, Country Meadow, Lost Oaks, Oak Meadow, Oak Valley, Hide Away and Plantation. It is one of the older acreage communities in the area, and unlike the newer gated developments it has grown in — the trees are mature, the driveways are established, and it reads as a place people have lived for a long time.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **135 parcels covering roughly 449 acres**, with **126 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). Lot sizes: 10th percentile about **2.09 acres**, median **3.0 acres**, 90th percentile about **4.53 acres**. Three acres is the standard lot — smaller than River Mountain Ranch or Sabinas Creek Ranch, which keeps the price down while still giving real separation.

That combination — three wooded acres, an established neighborhood, under $700,000 at the median — is the reason to look here. Very little else in Kendall County offers it.

The association's filed management certificate records plats from **Unit 1 (Kendall County Document No. 1995-103575)** through **Unit 4 (Document No. 2005-199422)**. So the subdivision was platted starting in 1995 and expanded through 2005.

That matters for the housing stock: most homes here date from the late 1990s and 2000s. Expect the maintenance profile of a 20-to-30-year-old house — roofs, HVAC systems, water heaters, and septic systems that are at or past their first replacement cycle. Price that in.

We were not able to identify the original developer from a primary source.

## HOA

It is run by volunteer officers rather than a professional management company (TREC management certificate, filed September 2025).

The filed certificate discloses a **$250 first-request resale certificate fee**. The recurring dues amount is not disclosed — Texas certificates only require transfer-related fees — and we could not verify it. Contact the association's officers directly using the information on the filed certificate.

A volunteer-run association at this scale usually means low dues and limited services. Ask specifically who maintains the roads and whether they are county-maintained or private.

We could not verify water and wastewater service from a primary source. On three-acre lots in unincorporated Kendall County, **individual wells and septic systems are the expected arrangement**, but that is an inference and you should confirm it in writing for the specific property.

If it is a well and septic — and it almost certainly is — get the well log, depth, pump age, and a water quality test, plus the septic permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program. On 1990s-era systems this is not a formality.

East of Boerne off FM 3351. This is a moderate drive — further out than the in-town subdivisions, considerably closer in than River Mountain Ranch or Champee Springs. You are a reasonable run from Highway 46 and from I-10, which makes the San Antonio commute workable if not short.

name: Lost Creek
metaTitle: Lost Creek, Boerne TX 78015 — Guide, HOA, and the School District Trap
metaDescription: Lost Creek, Boerne 78015: 414 homes off Ralph Fair Road in Bexar County — and in NORTHSIDE ISD, not Boerne ISD. HOA, values, and the name collisions.
body:
Lost Creek is a large tract subdivision off Ralph Fair Road near I-10, built out in the second half of the 2000s. Its sections carry Spanish-mission names — Mission Bluff, Mission Haven, Mission Ledge, Mission Point, Mission Summit, Presidio Alley, Presidio Crest, Presidio Cliff, Presidio Sands — alongside Lost Creek Way and Lost Creek Gap.

It is one of the most affordable neighborhoods with a Boerne mailing address. It also carries the single most consequential misconception in this guide.

## The school district — this is NOT Boerne ISD

**Lost Creek is in Northside ISD.**

Multiple real estate sources describe Lost Creek as a Boerne ISD neighborhood. That is wrong, and we tested it carefully because the stakes are high.

1. **Bexar County's own school district GIS layer** returns **Northside ISD** for this location.
2. **Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder address lookup returns no assignment** for Lost Creek addresses. We probed **nine separate parcels** spread from the south end of the subdivision to the north — Lost Creek Way, Lost Creek Gap, Presidio Sands, Mission Haven, Mission Bluff, Mission Point, Presidio Crest, Presidio Cliff. **All nine came back outside Boerne ISD.**

If you are buying in the Boerne area specifically for Boerne ISD schools, **Lost Creek will not get you there.** A buyer who relies on a listing that says "Boerne ISD" and does not verify would find out at enrollment.

Northside ISD is a large, well-regarded district — this is not a knock on the schools. It is a factual correction about which district you are in. **Verify the specific campus assignment with Northside ISD directly.** We are not naming campuses we have not confirmed for this address.

Note how tight this boundary is: **Fallbrook and Sablechase, both roughly a mile away off Ralph Fair Road, are in Boerne ISD.** Lost Creek is not. A mile is the whole difference.

## Watch for two other Lost Creeks

The name collides badly:

- **Lost Creek Ranch Homeowners Association, Inc.** is a completely separate community in **Collin County** — Plano, in the Dallas metro, roughly 300 miles from here. It has its own filed management certificate. Nothing about it applies to Boerne.
- A third, unrelated **Lost Creek** subdivision exists near Loop 1604 and Judson Road in northeast Bexar County, zoned to North East ISD.

If you are reading HOA documents or reviews, confirm you are looking at the **Ralph Fair Road** community in Bexar County.

## County and jurisdiction

**Lost Creek is in Bexar County.** The association's management certificate states the subdivision location as Bexar County directly (Bexar County Document No. 20210309138). Bexar County parcel records carry the community under Bexar County Block 4711D, with situs zips predominantly **78015**.

Not the City of Boerne. Not Kendall County. Bexar County tax rates apply.

Whether the parcel sits in unincorporated Bexar County, the City of Boerne's extraterritorial jurisdiction, or Fair Oaks Ranch's ETJ we could not resolve. Ask Bexar County for the specific address.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records for the CB 4711 Lost Creek sections show **414 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 0.148 acres** and a **median total appraised value near $368,000**. Construction runs **2006 through 2017, with a median year built of 2008** (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

At a median around $368,000, **Lost Creek is one of the most affordable neighborhoods in this guide** with a Boerne mailing address — second only to Silver Hills and Spencer Ranch. If your budget is the binding constraint and Boerne ISD is not a requirement, this deserves a look.

## Housing stock

Production tract homes from **Centex and Pulte**, built across the 2006-2017 window in sections marketed as The Bluffs of Lost Creek, Presidio of Lost Creek, The Summit of Lost Creek and The Hills of Lost Creek.

With a 2008 median build year, these homes are now approaching twenty. Original roofs, water heaters, and first HVAC systems are at or past replacement age. Budget for it and inspect accordingly — at this price point, a $15,000 deferred-maintenance surprise is a much bigger proportion of the deal than it would be at $900,000.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Lost Creek Homeowners Association, Inc.**, managed by **Spectrum Association Management** of San Antonio.

The filed certificate discloses closing costs: a **$200 administrative transfer fee**, a **$375 resale package fee**, and a **working capitalization fee equal to two months' assessments**.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** in dollar terms — which is worth noting, because the working capital fee is defined as two months of it. Get the current monthly or annual assessment from Spectrum Association Management directly; you need it to compute your closing costs as well as your carrying cost.

## Amenities and gating

We could not confirm an amenity package or gating from a primary source. Verify what exists before assuming.

## Utilities

Not confirmed from a primary source. Confirm the water and wastewater provider in writing for the specific property.

## Location and commute

Off Ralph Fair Road near I-10 West, roughly Exit 550. Interstate access is immediate and the San Antonio commute is short — genuinely one of the better commuter positions in this guide.

Downtown Boerne is fifteen minutes or so up the interstate.

## Who it suits

It suits a budget-conscious buyer who wants a short San Antonio commute, a Boerne mailing address, and the lowest entry price in the 78015 corridor, and who is comfortable with a 2006-2017 tract home that needs some attention. It suits investors looking at rental yield in a high-demand commute corridor.

It does not suit a family relocating for Boerne ISD — this is Northside ISD. It does not suit someone wanting acreage or Hill Country character. And it does not suit a buyer who skips a thorough inspection on a house at the twenty-year mark.

name: Menger Springs
metaTitle: Menger Springs, Boerne TX — Neighborhood Guide, HOA, Schools
metaDescription: Menger Springs, Boerne: 246 estate parcels inside city limits, Kendall County. HOA fees, lot sizes, schools, and the name confusion to avoid.
body:
Menger Springs is Boerne's inside-the-city-limits estate neighborhood, and that combination is rare enough to be its whole identity. Almost every community around here offering acre-plus lots under oak canopy is out in unincorporated Kendall County on a well and a septic field. Menger Springs is not.

The street names all end the same way — Bitter Springs, Cabin Springs, Creek Springs, Dobie Springs, Fair Springs, Fall Springs, Hollow Springs, Knoll Springs, Ledge Springs — which makes the neighborhood easy to recognize on a listing and slightly confusing to navigate the first time.

## First, the name problem

There are two entirely different things in Boerne called Menger Springs, and conflating them is the most common error published about this neighborhood.

1. **Menger Springs, the residential subdivision** — the gated estate community described here.
2. **Morningside at Menger Springs** — a Morningside Ministries continuing-care senior living campus along Menger Creek.

They are unrelated. A web search for "Menger Springs Boerne" surfaces the senior-living campus far more often than the subdivision. If someone tells you they are looking at Menger Springs, establish which one before you go any further.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **246 parcels across roughly 366 acres**, with **224 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). At 91% built out, this is a mature, nearly finished neighborhood.

The lot distribution is the interesting part: 10th percentile about **0.19 acres**, median **1.18 acres**, 90th percentile about **3.4 acres**. That is an enormous spread, and it tells you the community contains at least two distinct products — a garden-home or patio-home component on small lots, and an estate component on one to three-plus acres. Those are different neighborhoods with different buyers sharing one entrance.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels reflect the same split: **median near $1,098,000**, but with the 10th percentile down at roughly $481,000 and the 90th up at roughly $1,557,000. Appraisal-district values, not list prices. When you see a wide band like that, it is not noise — it is two products.

## Housing stock

Custom and semi-custom homes rather than production tract. Local builders active here over the years have included several Boerne-area custom shops. Prevailing style is Hill Country traditional: limestone, heavy timber accents, metal roofs, deep porches. Lots kept a lot of their original oak cover, which is the reason many buyers choose it over a newer development where the trees are ten years old.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on all 246 parcels. That is the headline fact. You get an acre or more of oak-covered land with **city water and sewer**, city police, and city services — without the well, the septic system, the volunteer fire response times, or the county permitting process that come with comparable acreage out in the county.

You also get the city tax line, which the unincorporated acreage communities do not have. That is the trade. For a lot of buyers it is a trade worth making.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Menger Springs Homeowners Association**, managed by FirstService Residential out of Dallas (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County Instrument #409303, filed June 12, 2026).

The filed certificate discloses a detailed and fairly aggressive fee schedule at closing: an **ownership transfer fee of $340**, a **resale certificate at $375 / $450 / $500 depending on turnaround speed**, a $75 resale certificate update, refinance certificates from $125 to $275, a $100 loan estimate questionnaire, a $150 HOA questionnaire, and a $150 reverse mortgage questionnaire. These stack up. If you are refinancing or selling, budget for them.

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the management certificate and we could not verify it from a primary source. Get it from FirstService Residential directly.

One oddity worth flagging for your title company: the certificate's own text lists the declaration recording data as being in the Official Public Records of **Bexar** County while the subdivision itself is unambiguously in Kendall County. That is most likely a clerical artifact on the filing, but have title confirm which instrument actually governs.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries then, and Menger Springs is large enough in extent that the ends of it could differ.

## Location and commute

Close in. You are near I-10 and a short run from downtown Boerne and the main retail corridor. For a neighborhood that feels this rural once you are inside the gate, the drive times are genuinely short — that is the unusual thing about it.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants an acre or more, oak trees, and a custom home, but does not want a well, a septic system, or a twenty-minute drive to a grocery store. It suits someone who wants the estate feel with city infrastructure underneath it.

It does not suit a buyer chasing the lowest tax rate — you are paying city taxes for city services. It does not suit someone who wants a resort amenity package; the amenity here is the land. And it does not suit a buyer who assumes every lot in the neighborhood is an acre. Check the actual lot size on the specific property, because a meaningful share of Menger Springs is well under half an acre.

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you want current Menger Springs listings, or help telling the estate sections from the garden-home sections before you tour, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

body:
Miralomas is a newer development west of Boerne off the Highway 46 corridor, in the same general area as Tapatio Springs and Indian Springs. The street names run to birds and Spanish — Alba, Canario, Hibiscus, Ibis, Mancha, Mariposa, Mockingbird, Monarca. It is one of the more actively building communities on the west side of town.

There is a genuine inconsistency in the public record for Miralomas, and you should know about it.

**Kendall County Appraisal District appraises all 268 Miralomas parcels as Kendall County property**, with Kendall County as the county taxing unit and Boerne ISD as the school district (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). The parcels sit at roughly 29.76 N, 98.80 W — well northwest of the Bexar County line. Bexar County's own parcel records return no Miralomas properties.

**However**, the Miralomas Property Owners Association's management certificate was recorded in the Official Public Records of **Bexar** County.

The most likely explanation is that the association's governing documents were recorded in Bexar County for reasons tied to the developer's entity rather than to the land's location, or that the filing is simply misplaced. **The appraisal district's determination of county is the one that governs your tax bill**, and it says Kendall.

Practical instruction: have your title company confirm which recorded instruments actually govern the property and in which county's records they sit. Do not let a listing or an HOA document's recording county override what the appraisal district says about where the land is.

## The numbers

Kendall CAD parcel records show **268 parcels covering roughly 182 acres**, with only **104 currently improved** (retrieved September 2026). That is 39% built out — this is an actively developing community, and you will have construction around you.

The community's own marketing describes a footprint of nearly 900 acres with more than half preserved as undeveloped nature, so the 182 platted acres above represent what has been recorded so far, not the eventual size.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.129 acres**, median **0.204 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.552 acres**. Builders have marketed 55-foot and 65-foot lot widths in the Mariposa ridgeline section.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $604,000**, 10th percentile around $494,000, 90th around $870,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

New construction from a mix of builders — Sitterle Homes, Prestige Homes and David Weekley Homes have all been active here, with David Weekley building a section marketed as The Summit at Miralomas. Expect current-generation plans, design center finishes, and builder warranties.

## The utility district — a real cost and a real feature

Miralomas is served by the **Miralomas Municipal Utility District**, which purchases potable water from the Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority and operates its own low-pressure wastewater collection system and treatment plant. The plant produces **reclaimed non-potable water piped to every lot for irrigation**.

That reclaimed-water irrigation system is genuinely unusual and genuinely valuable in a drought-prone county — outdoor watering restrictions that hit municipal customers work differently when your irrigation supply is reclaimed effluent.

But a MUD is a **taxing entity**. There is a district levy on the tax bill that a home inside Boerne city limits with plain city utilities does not carry. We were not able to verify the current district rate from the district's own filing, so **pull the actual MUD rate and model the full tax bill before you underwrite a payment.** This is the single largest variable in what Miralomas actually costs per month, and it is the one most often left out of a comparison against, say, Regent Park or Champion Heights.

## Jurisdiction

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Miralomas parcels. This is **unincorporated Kendall County** — outside the City of Boerne. County sheriff, county permitting, plus the MUD for water and wastewater.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Miralomas Property Owners Association, Inc.**, managed by Goodwin & Company.

The filed certificate discloses closing-table charges: a **$300 working capital fee**, a **$375 resale certificate**, and a **$340 transfer fee**.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate. Get it from Goodwin & Company directly — and get the MUD rate at the same time, because the two together are your real monthly number.

## Amenities

The community markets hiking trails, a 40-acre lake, a fitness center, a pool and a clubhouse. At 39% built out, verify which of these are actually open. Amenity delivery at partially built communities frequently lags the marketing.

We found no source describing Miralomas as gated.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). Confirm your specific address; boundaries were redrawn in August 2024 and a still-growing community may see future changes.

## Location and commute

West Boerne off Highway 46. Further from I-10 than the south-side neighborhoods, which makes the San Antonio commute longer. Downtown Boerne and the H-E-B are reasonable drives.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants new construction with real open space and an unusual, drought-resilient irrigation setup, and who does the math on the MUD levy with eyes open. It suits people who want west-side Boerne and a natural setting.

It does not suit a commuter who needs quick interstate access. It does not suit a buyer who wants a finished neighborhood — 61% of lots are still unbuilt. And it does not suit anyone comparing list prices across Boerne without accounting for the utility district tax.

metaDescription: Napa Oaks, Boerne 78015: 368 homes in Bexar County near Fair Oaks Parkway. Gated, Boerne ISD, Van Raub Elementary. HOA, values, and the name mix-up.
body:
Napa Oaks is a gated subdivision off I-10 near Fair Oaks Parkway, on the ridge above the interstate. The hilltop position gives parts of the neighborhood long views south toward San Antonio, which is the main thing people remember about it.

## One quick disambiguation

There is a **Napa Oaks apartment complex** on Napa Landing in the Boerne area, and there is **Napa Oaks the single-family gated subdivision**. They share a name and they are not the same property. If you are searching listings or reading reviews, check which one you are looking at.

## County and jurisdiction

**Napa Oaks is in Bexar County.** The Napa Oaks Owners' Association's management certificate lists all subdivision plats — Units 1 through 7 plus 2A, 3.1, 6A and 6B — as recorded in the **Official Deed and Plat Records of Bexar County, Texas** (Bexar County Document No. 20220180234, filed July 22, 2022). Bexar County parcel records carry all 368 parcels.

The mailing address is **Boerne, TX 78015**. That is postal geography, not political geography. This is **not** the City of Boerne and **not** Kendall County. Your county tax rate is Bexar County's.

We could not confirm whether the neighborhood sits in unincorporated Bexar County or within a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction. Ask Bexar County for the specific address if permitting matters to you.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **368 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 0.198 acres** (10th percentile 0.15, 90th percentile roughly 0.33 acres) and a **median total appraised value near $530,000** (10th percentile around $415,000, 90th around $720,000). Construction runs from roughly 2010 through 2024 (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

At a median around $530,000, Napa Oaks sits below Front Gate and Fallbrook and well below Balcones Creek in appraised value — which makes it one of the more accessible gated options in the 78015 corridor.

## Housing stock

Production single-family homes. The earliest declaration of covenants, for Unit 1, was executed **November 23, 2009**, with later phases platted through the mid-2010s. Brightland Homes has been active here more recently.

Reported square footages span roughly **1,610 to 3,963 square feet**, which is a wide range — this neighborhood contains genuinely different house sizes, from modest to substantial. Know which section you are in.

Because the build window spans 2010 to 2024, the older sections are now in the range where roofs, water heaters and first HVAC systems come due. The newer sections are not. That difference should show up in your offer.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Napa Oaks Owners' Association, Inc.**, managed by FirstService Residential from its San Antonio office on Huebner Road — the same office that manages Balcones Creek and Fallbrook.

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the management certificate, and secondary sources vary widely, citing figures from $186 per quarter to $450 per year for individual properties. Those are inconsistent enough that none of them should be relied on. **Get the current assessment in writing from FirstService Residential.**

## Amenities and gating

The community is described as gated — one description calls it "double gated," which likely refers to separate gated sections within the neighborhood. We could not confirm whether gates are staffed or automated.

There is a **community pool** off Napa Landing, positioned to take advantage of the long views toward San Antonio.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** Bexar County's own school district GIS layer returns Boerne ISD for this location, and Boerne ISD's InfoFinder address lookup returns **Van Raub Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** (both queried September 2026).

Note that Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in August 2024 when Viola Wilson Elementary opened, and Van Raub was one of the campuses that received relief from that change. Verify your specific address with the district.

## Utilities

Not independently confirmed. Confirm the water and wastewater provider in writing for the specific property. On fifth-acre lots in this corridor, a central system is likely, but "likely" is not a basis for a purchase decision.

## Location and commute

Off I-10 near Fair Oaks Parkway. Interstate access is immediate, which makes this among the best commuter positions in this guide. Northwest San Antonio retail and medical are close. Downtown Boerne is a drive — you are in the 78015 corridor, not in the town.

The ridge position that gives the views also means some lots are close to I-10. Highway noise carries uphill. Stand in the backyard on a weekday before you commit.

## Who it suits

It suits a commuter who wants a gated neighborhood, a pool, Boerne ISD schools, and a view, at a price below most of the surrounding gated communities. It suits buyers who want proximity to San Antonio more than proximity to Boerne.

It does not suit someone who wants acreage or the Hill Country setting. It does not suit a buyer sensitive to traffic noise without checking the specific lot. And it does not suit anyone assuming a Boerne mailing address means Kendall County taxes — it does not.

metaDescription: Ranger Creek, Boerne: 395 parcels west of town off I-10, unincorporated Kendall County, no mandatory HOA on file. Lot sizes, schools, commute.
body:
Ranger Creek is an older, loosely platted community west of Boerne along the I-10 corridor, with streets named for birds and Hill Country features — Arrowhead, Blue Heron, Blue Jay, Deer, Doeskin, Dove, Eagle, Flintrock, North View. It does not look like a modern subdivision and it was not built like one. Houses vary widely in age, size and condition, lots vary in size, and the overall feel is closer to a rural community that grew than a development that was planned.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **395 parcels covering roughly 400 acres**, with **373 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). At 94% built out, this is a long-established community.

Lot sizes: 10th percentile about **0.345 acres**, median **0.525 acres**, 90th percentile about **1.78 acres**. Half an acre is typical, with a meaningful tail of larger lots.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $383,000**, 10th percentile around $277,000, 90th around $577,000.

That 10th percentile figure is the story. **At roughly $277,000, Ranger Creek has the lowest entry point of any community in this guide.** If your budget is genuinely constrained and you want a Kendall County address with Boerne ISD schools, this is where to look. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## HOA status — unverified, and that cuts both ways

We searched the Texas Real Estate Commission's statewide HOA management certificate database and **found no filed management certificate for a Ranger Creek property owners association.**

Be careful how you read that. It is evidence, not proof:

- It may mean there is **no mandatory HOA** — plausible for a community of this vintage and character, and consistent with the variation you see driving through it.
- It may mean an association exists but has not complied with the Texas Property Code § 209.004 filing requirement.
- It may mean an association is indexed under a name we did not match.

What it does **not** mean is that the land is unrestricted. **Recorded deed restrictions run with the property whether or not an HOA exists to enforce them,** and neighbors have standing to enforce them in many cases. If you are buying here because you want to park an RV, run a business, or put up a metal building, get the actual recorded restrictions from your title company and read them. Do not rely on "no HOA."

Also ask about road maintenance. Where there is no association, private road upkeep is either a county responsibility or an informal arrangement among owners, and the latter is a recurring source of disputes.

## Housing stock

Highly variable. Because this community developed over decades rather than in phases, you will find small older homes, manufactured housing, substantial custom builds, and everything between, sometimes on the same street. Condition varies as much as style.

This is a neighborhood where the individual property matters far more than the neighborhood average, and where a thorough inspection is essential. Do not assume a value from a comp two streets over.

## Utilities

Not verified. Expect **wells and septic** on the larger lots; some parts of the community may be on a shared or community water system given the half-acre typical lot size. Confirm in writing for the specific property, and get the septic permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program. On older properties, unpermitted or long-expired septic systems are a real possibility — check.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Ranger Creek parcels. **Unincorporated Kendall County** — no city property tax, no city services, county sheriff, rural fire response.

The low tax rate is part of why the numbers work here.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Ranger Creek is spread out along the I-10 corridor and boundaries were redrawn in August 2024.

## Location and commute

West of Boerne along I-10. Interstate access is good, which makes the San Antonio commute workable. Downtown Boerne and the H-E-B are short drives. This is not a remote location, despite the rural feel.

The tradeoff is the interstate itself — some parts of the community are close enough to hear it. Stand in the yard.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer on a real budget who wants a Kendall County address, Boerne ISD schools, half an acre, and a workable commute, and who is prepared to buy an older property and evaluate it on its own merits. It suits people who want fewer rules and are willing to accept fewer guarantees about what the neighbors do.

It does not suit a buyer who wants uniformity, covenant enforcement, or a predictable comp set. It does not suit someone who wants a new house. And it does not suit anyone who hears "no HOA on file" and assumes the land is unrestricted — get the title work and read it.

metaTitle: Regent Park, Boerne TX — Neighborhood Guide, HOA, Schools
metaDescription: Regent Park, Boerne: 484 homes inside City of Boerne limits off I-10. HOA fees, amenities, schools, and the San Antonio name confusion to avoid.
body:
Regent Park sits just off Interstate 10 on the south side of Boerne, close enough that the commute argument makes itself. The streets carry English and French names — Balmoral, Bretford, Cheslyn, Fanwick, Giverny, Haverton, Alcantara — on a conventional curvilinear plan with sidewalks and a community amenity center.

## Clearing up a name collision first

There is a **Regent Park in Shavano Park / San Antonio 78231** with its own homeowners association, and searching for "Regent Park HOA" will surface it. It is a different place.

The Boerne Regent Park has its own separate association whose plats — Units 1 through 4 and their phases — are recorded in the **Deed and Plat Records of Kendall County, Texas** (TREC management certificate for Regent Park Homeowners Association, Inc.). If you are reading HOA documents, make sure the recording county says Kendall.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **484 parcels across roughly 171 acres**, with **454 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). Roughly 94% built out, though new construction has continued in the later units.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.152 acres**, median **0.197 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.287 acres**. Builders market these as 50-foot and 60-foot lot widths.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $559,000**, 10th percentile around $449,000, 90th around $715,000. Appraisal-district values, not list prices.

## Housing stock

Production new construction from several national and regional builders — Highland Homes, Brightland Homes, M/I Homes, Kindred Homes and Journey Homes have all been active here. Plans run from modest single-story homes up through larger two-story plans with game rooms and studies. Elevations are stone-and-stucco in the current regional idiom.

Because the neighborhood has built out in units over several years, the earlier sections have grown-in landscaping and the newer sections do not. That is a visible difference on a tour and a real one in July.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on all 484 parcels. This is inside the city limits — city water and sewer, city trash, Boerne PD, and a city tax line on the bill. No well, no septic, no utility district levy. Compared with Esperanza, which is unincorporated and served by a water control and improvement district, Regent Park's tax structure is the more conventional of the two. Run the actual numbers on both before assuming which is cheaper.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Regent Park Homeowners Association, Inc.**, managed by Great America Companies of San Antonio (TREC management certificate, plats recorded Kendall County).

The filed certificate discloses the closing-table charges specifically: a **$250 transfer fee**, a **$500 capitalization fee**, a **$100 resale certificate fee**, a **$50 refinance fee**, and a **$25 statement of account fee**. Those are clear and reasonable.

**The recurring annual assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate. A secondary source puts it in the range of $900 to $977 per year, but that is unverified and we would not publish it as fact. Confirm the current assessment with Great America Companies before your option period ends.

## Amenities

This is one of Regent Park's stronger cards. The community has a **pool, a recreation building with an exercise room, a party pavilion, a playground, walking trails, and community parks**. For a neighborhood in this price band inside Boerne city limits, that is a fuller amenity package than most — Saddlehorn, the Woods of Boerne, and the Woods of Frederick Creek have nothing comparable.

We found no source describing Regent Park as gated, and its location inside city limits suggests public streets. Verify if it matters to you.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Kendall Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address. Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries when Viola Wilson Elementary opened in August 2024, and nearby Kendall Creek Estates — barely two miles away — now feeds Viola Wilson rather than Kendall Elementary. Boundaries in this part of the district are genuinely in motion.

## Location and commute

Directly off I-10, roughly three miles from downtown Boerne. This is one of the best commuter positions in Kendall County: you are on the interstate almost immediately, and you are still close enough to town that the H-E-B and the Hill Country Mile are short trips.

The tradeoff is interstate proximity. Some lots are closer to I-10 than others and there is road noise. Stand in the backyard before you decide.

## Who it suits

It suits a commuter who wants new construction, a pool and a gym, a Boerne address with city utilities, and the shortest practical drive to San Antonio. It suits families who want amenities without Esperanza's scale or utility district.

It does not suit a buyer who wants acreage, trees, or quiet — this is suburban and close-set. It does not suit someone sensitive to highway noise without checking the specific lot. And it does not suit anyone who wants the historic Boerne character.

name: River Mountain Ranch
metaTitle: River Mountain Ranch, Boerne TX — Guide, HOA, Schools, Well & Septic
metaDescription: River Mountain Ranch, Boerne: 563 acreage tracts on 3,100 acres, voluntary POA, private Guadalupe river parks. Wells, septic, schools, real commute.
body:
River Mountain Ranch is out FM 474 — Blanco Road — east of Boerne, past Cave Without a Name, off Kreutzberg Road. It is one of the largest acreage subdivisions in Kendall County and it does not feel like a neighborhood at all. Streets like Kreutzberg, Hoskins Trail, Clear Creek, Clear Springs, Red Oak, North Star and Brookview run through cedar and oak with long gaps between mailboxes.

Horses are normal here. So are tractors, hay, and gates you open yourself.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **563 parcels covering roughly 3,104 acres**, with **467 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). That is a big community by land area — more than half the footprint of Cordillera Ranch — with far fewer amenities and far lower prices.

Lot sizes: 10th percentile about **3.07 acres**, median **5.0 acres**, 90th percentile about **7.9 acres**. Five acres is the standard tract.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $780,000**, 10th percentile around $563,000, 90th around $1,166,000. Appraisal-district values, not list prices. For five acres with private Guadalupe access, that is among the better value-per-acre propositions in the county — and the reason for it is the drive, which we will get to.

## The HOA is voluntary — and that is a genuinely important distinction

Almost every community in this guide has a mandatory HOA. River Mountain Ranch does not.

The **River Mountain Ranch Property Owners Association** is a **voluntary** association, run by a volunteer elected board rather than a management company. Its filed management certificate lists a residential mailing address in Boerne and an individual board president as the designated representative, with a $200 transfer fee (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County Instrument #371843, filed July 7, 2022). The association's site is rmrpoa.com.

What voluntary means in practice:

- **You are not automatically obligated to pay dues** the way you would be in a mandatory-membership subdivision.
- **The river parks are a members' amenity.** If you do not join, you should not assume you get access. This is the practical consequence most buyers miss — people buy here *for* the river and then discover access is tied to membership in an association they thought was optional.
- **Deed restrictions still apply regardless.** Voluntary POA membership does not mean no rules. The recorded restrictions govern the land whether you join or not.

Before you write an offer, get in writing: what membership costs, what it includes, whether the seller is current, and exactly what river park access requires.

## The river parks

The community's amenity is **three private river parks on the Guadalupe**, with grills and picnic areas, used for tubing, kayaking, and fishing. The parks are gated.

Note the distinction carefully: **the river parks are gated. Whether the subdivision entrance itself is gated is a separate question** and we could not confirm it from a primary source. "Gated river parks" and "gated community" are different claims, and they get conflated constantly in listings. Verify on the ground.

Individual lots generally do not front the river.

## Utilities — wells and septic, plan accordingly

River Mountain Ranch is on **individual water wells and on-site septic systems**. There is no central water or sewer out here.

That is not a dealbreaker — thousands of Kendall County households live this way — but it changes your inspection list and your budget. Get the well log, well depth, pump age, pressure tank condition, and a bacteriological and mineral water test. Get the septic system's permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program and have the tank pumped and inspected. On a five-acre property, a failing septic field or a marginal well is a five-figure problem, and it will not show up on a standard home inspection.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit**. This is **unincorporated Kendall County**, well outside any City of Boerne boundary. No city tax, no city services, county sheriff, rural fire response. Confirm your homeowner's insurance carrier is comfortable with the ISO fire rating out here — it affects premiums.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Curington Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Across 3,100 acres, zoning can differ at the extremes, and Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in August 2024.

The school bus ride from out here is long. Factor it honestly into the decision if you have young children.

## Location and commute

From downtown Boerne: east on FM 474 roughly six miles, then Kreutzberg Road. It is a beautiful drive and a slow one. There is no quick way to make it faster.

To I-10 and then San Antonio, this is a substantial daily commute. To the H-E-B, it is a planned trip, not an errand. Cell coverage is uneven in the low spots.

## Who it suits

It suits someone who wants five acres, a horse or two, real quiet, and a piece of the Guadalupe, at a price that acreage closer to town does not reach. It suits people who work remotely or on a flexible schedule. It suits buyers comfortable maintaining their own water and waste systems.

It does not suit a daily San Antonio commuter, a family that wants sidewalks and a short bus ride, or a buyer who wants an HOA to handle things — here, largely, nobody does. And it does not suit someone who assumed river access came automatically with the deed.

## Talk to someone who works this market

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you want current River Mountain Ranch listings, or help understanding exactly what POA membership costs and what it gets you on the river, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

name: Sabinas Creek Ranch
metaTitle: Sabinas Creek Ranch, Boerne TX — Guide, HOA, Well & Septic, Schools
metaDescription: Sabinas Creek Ranch, Boerne: 130 acreage lots on 774 acres, gated, unincorporated Kendall County, wells and septic. HOA fees, schools, commute.
body:
Sabinas Creek Ranch is a gated acreage community north of Boerne, up FM 474 past where the town thins out. Streets include Sabinas Ridge, Sabinas Springs, Megan Ridge, Phillip Ranch, Spalten Ridge, Taylor Ridge and Wainright Springs. It is newer than most acreage subdivisions in the county, and it shows — paved roads, engineered entries, and a lot of very recent custom construction.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **130 parcels covering roughly 774 acres**, with only **79 currently improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). At 61% built out, this is the least-finished acreage community in this guide — meaning a meaningful share of what trades here is still raw lots, and you will have construction as a neighbor for years.

Lot sizes: 10th percentile about **3.23 acres**, median **5.01 acres**, 90th percentile about **10.19 acres**. Five acres is the standard.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $1,335,000**, 10th percentile around $1,045,000, 90th around $1,978,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices. Note how high the 10th percentile sits — there is essentially no entry-level product here. The architectural standards and the lot cost put a floor under it.

## Housing stock

Custom and semi-custom homes on acreage, most built within the last decade. Journey Homes has marketed "Hill Country Series" and "Estate Series" product lines here. Prevailing style is contemporary Hill Country — limestone, metal roofs, large windows, the current regional vocabulary rather than the heavier 1990s look you see in older acreage subdivisions.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Sabinas Creek Ranch Property Owners Association**, managed by FirstService Residential San Antonio (TREC management certificate, plats recorded Kendall County).

The filed certificate discloses closing costs: a **$375 resale certificate fee**, a **$340 transfer fee**, and a **$150 refinance fee**.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate and we could not verify it from a primary source. Get it from FirstService Residential directly. On a gated community with private paved roads, the assessment typically has to fund road maintenance, and road reserves are worth asking about specifically — ask whether the association has a funded reserve study for repaving.

## Utilities — wells and septic

Sabinas Creek Ranch is on **individual water wells and on-site septic systems**. Listing utility data for properties here identifies well water and septic sewer, with Bandera Electric Cooperative for power.

Treat that as a core part of your diligence, not a footnote. Get the well log and depth, the pump and pressure tank age, and both a bacteriological and a mineral water test. Get the septic permit history from Kendall County's on-site sewage program and have the system inspected and pumped. Aerobic systems require ongoing maintenance contracts — find out which type is installed.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Sabinas Creek Ranch parcels. This is **unincorporated Kendall County** — no city property tax, no city services. County sheriff, county permitting, rural fire response. The absence of a city tax line is a genuine and recurring savings; the absence of city fire protection is a genuine and recurring insurance consideration. Get a quote before you are under contract.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Curington Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in August 2024, and Sabinas Creek Ranch sits far enough north that boundary questions are reasonable.

## Location and commute

From Boerne, Highway 46 to Esser Road north, which becomes FM 474. The community is roughly eight and a half miles from downtown Boerne. That is a real drive for groceries and a real drive for school, and the run to I-10 and then San Antonio is longer still.

The upside is what that distance buys: quiet, dark skies, and five acres of Hill Country without a neighbor's roofline in your view.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer building or buying a custom home on acreage who wants a gated entrance, paved roads, and architectural standards protecting the value of what they build. It suits people who want newer construction rather than a 1990s acreage home.

It does not suit a commuter with a fixed early start in San Antonio. It does not suit a buyer who wants a finished neighborhood — nearly 40% of the lots are still vacant and construction traffic is part of the deal. It does not suit anyone uncomfortable owning a well and a septic system. And it does not suit a buyer at the lower end of the Boerne market; there is no inexpensive way into this one.

body:
Sablechase is a gated subdivision off Old Fredericksburg Road near Ralph Fair Road, reached from I-10 West. It is one of the larger and slightly older communities in the 78015 corridor, and at a median appraised value just above $500,000 it is among the more accessible gated options in the area.

**Sablechase is in Bexar County.** The SA Sablechase Homeowners Association's amended management certificate records the Declaration of Covenants under Bexar County Document No. 20080050593, with amendments and supplemental declarations for Units 1, 2, 3A and 3C all likewise in the **Official Public Records of Bexar County, Texas** (Bexar County Document No. 20230230820, filed December 20, 2023). Bexar County parcel records carry all 508 parcels.

The mailing address is **Boerne, TX 78015** — postal geography. This is **not** the City of Boerne and **not** Kendall County. Bexar County tax rates apply, and there is no City of Boerne tax or service.

We could not confirm whether the neighborhood is in unincorporated Bexar County or inside a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction; no source places it inside an incorporated city.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **508 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 0.212 acres** (10th percentile 0.17, 90th percentile roughly 0.32 acres) and a **median total appraised value near $514,000** (10th percentile around $415,000, 90th around $655,000). Construction runs from roughly 2010 through 2018 (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

The build window is worth noting: Sablechase finished around **2018**, earlier than Fallbrook or Front Gate, which are still adding homes. That makes this a **finished neighborhood** — no construction traffic, mature-enough landscaping, and a settled community. It also means the oldest homes here are now approaching sixteen years, and first-replacement items are coming due.

The original Declaration was recorded in **2008** (Document No. 20080050593), with a first amendment the same year and supplemental declarations for Unit 2 in 2011, Unit 3A in 2012, and Unit 3C in 2013.

Some marketing copy dates the community to 2010. The recorded declaration says 2008. Trust the filing.

**Pool, sports courts, playground, barbecue areas and a clubhouse.** The community is consistently described as gated; we could not confirm whether the gates are staffed or automated.

Verify your specific address. Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries then, with Van Raub among the affected campuses.

And a warning specific to this corridor: **Lost Creek, roughly a mile away off Ralph Fair Road, is not in Boerne ISD at all — it is Northside ISD.** District boundaries here do not follow the roads or the zip code in any intuitive way. Do not assume a neighboring subdivision's schools apply to yours.

Not independently confirmed. Confirm the water and wastewater provider in writing for the specific property.

Off Old Fredericksburg Road near Ralph Fair Road, about two miles from the I-10 West Ralph Fair exit. Interstate access is quick and the San Antonio commute is short.

## Who it suits

body:
Saddlehorn is small, tight, and one of the more attainable places to buy a house with a Boerne address inside the city limits. Every street is named for a racetrack — Belmont, Churchill, Del Mar, Derby, Dover Downs, Pocono, Santa Anita, Retama — which is the kind of detail you only notice once and then never forget.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **140 parcels across roughly 32 acres**, with **132 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). That is 94% built out on a very small footprint. Thirty-two acres for 140 homes tells you most of what you need to know about density.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.111 acres**, median **0.129 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.217 acres**. These are small lots — roughly an eighth of an acre is typical.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $401,000**, 10th percentile around $349,000, 90th around $467,000. That is the narrowest value band of any neighborhood in this guide, and among the lowest. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

A tight band like that is actually useful information for a buyer: it means homes here are similar to one another, appraisals are predictable, and you are unlikely to overpay by accident or find a hidden bargain. It is an efficient little market.

## Housing stock

Conventional single-family production homes. The plat record includes both Saddlehorn Subdivision and a later phase called The Reserve at Saddlehorn (recorded in Kendall County plat records at Volume 7, Pages 53-55 and Volume 8, Pages 74-75 respectively, per the association's filed management certificate). Expect one- and two-story plans, attached front garages, modest front yards.

We were not able to verify square footage ranges or the original builder from a primary source. Saddlehorn has one of the thinnest public data trails of any established neighborhood in Boerne — there is no community website, no developer marketing page still standing, and very little written about it. Judge it by walking it rather than by reading about it.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on all 140 parcels. Inside the city limits: city water and sewer, city trash, Boerne PD, and a city tax line. On eighth-acre lots, city utilities are exactly what you want.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Boerne Saddlehorn Homeowners Association, Inc.**, a Texas nonprofit corporation operating from a P.O. box in Boerne (TREC management certificate, Kendall County). Unlike most neighborhoods in this guide it is not run by an outside management company, which typically means lower overhead and slower response times.

The filed certificate discloses a **$250 resale certificate processing fee**. The recurring dues amount is not disclosed — Texas management certificates only require transfer-related fees — and we could not verify it from any primary source. **Contact the association directly** using the email on the filed certificate before your option period ends. Do not rely on a dues figure from a listing aggregator.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Curington Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your address with the district. Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries at that time, so any school claim on an older listing or blog post may be out of date.

## Location and commute

Central. Saddlehorn sits well inside Boerne, which is the entire argument for it. You are close to schools, close to the H-E-B, close to downtown and the Hill Country Mile, and a straightforward run to I-10 for a San Antonio commute. For a price band this low, that location is unusual — most comparably priced inventory in the area is either further out or in Bexar County.

## Who it suits

It suits a first-time buyer, a downsizer, or an investor who wants a Boerne address and Boerne ISD schools at the bottom of the local price range, with city utilities and a short drive to everything. It suits someone who wants low maintenance — an eighth of an acre is a yard you mow in twenty minutes.

It does not suit anyone who wants land, privacy, or distance from neighbors. It does not suit a buyer expecting an amenity package; we found no pool or clubhouse.
