name: Silver Hills
metaTitle: Silver Hills, Boerne TX — Guide, Two-County Split, POA, Schools
metaDescription: Silver Hills near Bergheim: a subdivision genuinely split between Kendall and Comal counties, platted 1966-67. POA, wells and septic, school zones.
body:
Silver Hills is a rural community southeast of Boerne along FM 3351 near Bergheim, on Silver Hills Drive and Desert Gold. It is one of the oldest platted subdivisions in the area, and it has a structural quirk that makes it worth a page of its own: **it straddles a county line.**

## The two-county split — confirmed, not a rumor

Silver Hills is genuinely divided between **Kendall County and Comal County**. This is not a mapping error or a mailing-address artifact. The evidence is two separate, currently-filed management certificates for the **same** association:

- A certificate recorded in **Kendall County**, referencing a plat filed **January 9, 1967** (Document 1967-6), with a covenant extension recorded May 27, 2025.
- A certificate recorded in **Comal County**, referencing a plat filed **December 23, 1966** (Document 84351), with a covenant extension recorded the same day, May 27, 2025, and filed with the Comal County Clerk.

Both list the same association president, the same P.O. box in Bergheim, and the same association website. The plats were filed within weeks of each other in late 1966 and early 1967 — one on each side of the line.

**What this means for a buyer:** which county a specific Silver Hills lot sits in determines your county tax rate, your county services, your permitting authority, and potentially your school district. You cannot answer any of those questions for "Silver Hills" as a whole. You have to answer them for the specific parcel. Start with the appraisal district record for that parcel ID.

## The numbers (Kendall County portion only)

Kendall County Appraisal District records show **19 Silver Hills parcels covering roughly 27 acres** on the Kendall side, with **15 improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). The Comal County portion is appraised by Comal CAD and is not included in those figures — so the community as a whole is larger than these numbers suggest.

On the Kendall side: lot sizes run a 10th percentile of about **0.26 acres**, a median of **1.13 acres**, and a 90th percentile of about **3.02 acres**.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved Kendall-side parcels: **median near $250,000**, 10th percentile around $169,000, 90th around $351,000.

Those are the **lowest values in this entire guide by a wide margin.** If your budget genuinely tops out well under $350,000 and you want land in the Boerne area, Silver Hills is one of the very few places that math works. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices, and the low figures reflect older and smaller housing stock.

## History and character

The Texas State Historical Association's Handbook of Texas describes Silver Hills as a rural community and notes that visible development probably began by the 1980s — roughly fifteen to twenty years after the plats were filed in 1966-67. That gap between platting and building is typical of speculative mid-century Hill Country subdivisions, and it explains the character: lots laid out on a 1960s plan, built out slowly and individually over decades.

Expect wide variation in housing age, size and condition. This is not a uniform neighborhood, and comps here need care.

## POA

**There is a mandatory association**: **Silver Hills Property Owners Association**, volunteer-run from a P.O. box in Bergheim, with CC&Rs described in its own filings as active and enforceable and extended by recorded instrument in May 2025.

The filed certificates disclose a **$150 resale certificate fee**, a **$75 updated resale certificate**, and a **$150 transfer certificate fee**.

**The recurring assessment is not disclosed.** Contact the association directly.

## Utilities

**Private wells and septic systems.** Individual listings in the community reference well water and septic service. Confirm for the specific property, and given the age of the housing stock, treat well and septic inspection as essential rather than optional. Systems here may date to the 1980s.

## Schools — genuinely unresolved on the Comal side

For the **Kendall County portion**, a point inside the community returns **Cibolo Creek Elementary, Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

For the **Comal County portion**, we could not resolve the assignment. Boerne ISD's boundary reaches into this area and Comal ISD also has presence nearby, and we are not going to guess which campus a Comal-side Silver Hills address attends.

**If schools matter to your decision, this is not a question to answer from a website — including this one.** Take the specific address to both districts and get it in writing.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on the Kendall-side parcels. Unincorporated, on both sides of the line. County sheriff, rural fire response, county permitting.

## Location and commute

FM 3351 southeast of Boerne near Bergheim. This is rural. The drive to Boerne for groceries or school is substantial, and the run to I-10 and San Antonio is longer still. Cell coverage is uneven.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer whose budget genuinely does not reach the rest of the Boerne market, who wants an acre of land, and who is prepared to buy an older home with old systems and fix things themselves. It suits people who want to be left alone.

It does not suit anyone who needs a short commute, a predictable comp set, new construction, or certainty about school assignment without doing the legwork. And it does not suit a buyer who will not verify which county their specific lot is in before making an offer — because that one fact changes the tax bill, the permitting, and possibly the schools.

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you are looking at a Silver Hills property and need the county line, tax rate, and school assignment nailed down for that specific parcel, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.

metaDescription: Southglen, Boerne: 432 homes inside City of Boerne limits, Kendall County — not Bexar, despite the 78015 zip. HOA, pool, schools, commute.
body:
Southglen sits on the south side of Boerne near Cascade Caverns Road, and its streets are relentlessly Scottish — Abbeydell, Aberdeen, Ayshire, Bellgrove, Braeburn, Breamoor, Clarendon, Edinburgh, Esslemont, Kilmarnock, Wickersham. It is a substantial, established subdivision that has recently seen new construction added to older phases, which makes it two neighborhoods in one.

## The county question — and why Southglen is the exception

Most homes with a **Boerne, TX 78015** mailing address are in **Bexar County**. Balcones Creek, Front Gate, Napa Oaks, Fallbrook, Sablechase, Anaqua Springs Ranch and Lost Creek are all Bexar County properties with Boerne mail.

**Southglen is not.** It is in **Kendall County**, and it is inside the **City of Boerne** city limits.

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show the County of Kendall and the **City of Boerne** as taxing units on all 432 Southglen parcels (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). Independently, the association's amended management certificate recorded in March 2026 cites every foundational document — the original declaration, multiple declarations of annexation, deeds without warranty, and even the swimming pool policies manual — as recorded in the **Official Public Records of Kendall County, Texas**.

Two independent sources, same answer. If you see Southglen described as a Bexar County neighborhood, that is wrong, and the difference shows up on the tax bill.

## The numbers

Kendall CAD parcel records show **432 parcels across roughly 117 acres**, with **391 already improved** (retrieved September 2026). Roughly 90% built out.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.122 acres**, median **0.153 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.279 acres**. Small suburban lots.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $432,000**, 10th percentile around $362,000, 90th around $523,000. That is one of the more affordable established neighborhoods inside Boerne city limits. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

Two distinct vintages. The original phases date back to an earlier era of the subdivision — the declaration carries an older-style Kendall County document number consistent with a 1990s filing — while a current phase is being built new by **Ashton Woods**, with plans running roughly 1,637 to 3,104 square feet in three to five bedroom configurations.

That split matters. A resale in an original phase and a new Ashton Woods home in the current phase are different products at different price points inside the same HOA. Know which one you are touring.

## Jurisdiction and utilities

Inside the **City of Boerne**, per Kendall CAD. That means City of Boerne water and sewer service and city trash, with Bandera Electric Cooperative serving power in this area. City police. A city tax line on the bill.

For a neighborhood on eighth-to-sixth-acre lots, city utilities are the right answer, and it is a meaningful advantage over comparably priced inventory further out.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Southglen Residential Community, Inc.**, a Texas nonprofit corporation. Note that the association's registered mailing address is in San Antonio 78258 — that is the management company's office, not the neighborhood's location. Do not read the management address as evidence of where the subdivision is; that mistake is exactly how Southglen gets mislabeled as a Bexar County community.

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the management certificate. A single resale listing cited $113 per quarter covering pool access, but that is one data point, not a confirmed fee schedule. Confirm the current assessment with the association before your option period ends.

## Amenities

Southglen has a **community pool** — the association's own filed certificate references a recorded Swimming Pool Policies and Procedures Manual, which is about as solid a confirmation as you get. Ashton Woods also markets a cabana, playscape, and hiking trails with the current phase.

Verify which amenities are available to which phases. In subdivisions that add new sections under a shared association, amenity access is occasionally phased too.

We found no source confirming the neighborhood is gated.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Kendall Elementary, Boerne Middle School South, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address. Boerne ISD opened Viola Wilson Elementary in August 2024 and redrew elementary boundaries then — and Southglen sits in the part of the district where that redraw was most active. Nearby Balcones Creek and Kendall Creek Estates both now feed Viola Wilson. A Southglen listing that names an elementary school without a date on the claim should not be trusted.

## Location and commute

South Boerne off Old Fredericksburg Road and Cascade Caverns Road, east of I-10. The interstate access is good, which makes the San Antonio commute among the more manageable ones from a Boerne address. Downtown Boerne and the Highway 46 retail corridor are short drives.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants an established Boerne address inside the city limits, a community pool, city utilities, and a price point below most of the newer Kendall County inventory. It suits commuters. It suits people who want to choose between a resale and a brand-new build without leaving the neighborhood.

It does not suit a buyer who wants land, trees, or privacy. It does not suit someone who wants uniformity — the old and new phases do not look alike. And it does not suit anyone underwriting a payment on the assumption that a 78015 address means Bexar County tax rates.

name: Spencer Ranch / The Birch at Spencer Ranch
metaTitle: Spencer Ranch / The Birch at Spencer Ranch, Boerne TX — Guide
metaDescription: Spencer Ranch and The Birch, Boerne: new D.R. Horton construction annexed into the City of Boerne. Road maintenance assessment, schools, what is coming.
body:
Spencer Ranch is the newest community in this guide, and it is still being built. The residential section under construction is marketed as **The Birch at Spencer Ranch** by D.R. Horton, on streets named Spencer Ranch, Hazel Peak, Mahogany Rapids and Sycamore Pond, off State Highway 46 on the west side of Boerne.

If you are reading this expecting an established neighborhood assessment, there is not one to give yet. What follows is what the public record actually shows.

## The numbers — early days

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **65 parcels covering roughly 29 acres**, with only **14 carrying an improvement** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). That is 22% built — the least-developed community in this guide.

Lots are small and uniform: 10th percentile about **0.12 acres**, median **0.13 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.23 acres**. Roughly an eighth of an acre, which is a dense, entry-level suburban product.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $325,000**, 10th percentile around $298,000, 90th around $459,000.

**That median is the second-lowest in this guide**, behind only Silver Hills. For new construction inside the City of Boerne with Boerne ISD schools, that is a genuinely notable entry point — and it is why this community is worth watching even though it is barely started.

Treat these figures with appropriate caution: with only 14 improved parcels on the roll, the statistics are drawn from a very small sample and will move as the community builds out.

## What is actually planned here

Local reporting and builder materials describe a larger project than the 29 platted acres currently on the appraisal roll:

- The Birch at Spencer Ranch is described as a **71-acre single-family phase** within a broader **183-acre residential project**.
- A separate **112-acre mixed-use component** has been discussed, with 560-plus low-rise multifamily units plus retail and office.
- The residential portion has been reported at **200-plus homes**.
- **Forestar Real Estate Group** is developing the land; **D.R. Horton** is building the homes.

**Take the multifamily and mixed-use component seriously as a buying consideration.** If you purchase a single-family home here, you should understand what is entitled to be built next to you. Ask the builder for the approved development plan and the zoning, and ask the City of Boerne planning department directly rather than relying on a sales office. A 560-unit apartment component adjacent to your house is the kind of thing that ought to be a known quantity before you sign, not a surprise in year three.

## Jurisdiction — annexed into the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on 64 of the 65 parcels. Local reporting has described the City annexing the Spencer Ranch land, which is consistent with the appraisal record.

So: inside the city limits, with City of Boerne utilities, city trash, Boerne PD, and a city property tax line. On eighth-acre lots, city water and sewer is the right arrangement.

## HOA — and an unusual line item

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Spencer Ranch Residential Community, Inc.**, managed by Vision Communities Management (TREC management certificate; Master Covenant recorded as Kendall County Instrument No. 2021-365072, Community Manual as Instrument No. 2022-365742).

The filed fee schedule, effective July 1, 2022, is unusually detailed and includes one item worth flagging:

- **Road Maintenance Assessment: $525.00**
- **Working Capital Assessment: $250.00**
- Resale Certificate: $340.00
- Transfer Fee: $250.00
- Statement of Account: $50.00
- Refinance Certificate: $50.00

A **Road Maintenance Assessment** on a community inside city limits is notable. It suggests some or all of the streets are **privately maintained by the association rather than by the City**, which means the HOA carries the long-term repaving obligation. Ask directly: which streets are public and which are private, and does the association hold a funded reserve for pavement?

**The recurring general assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate. Get it from Vision Communities Management along with the road maintenance answer.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address. Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in August 2024, and a community that is only 22% built is exactly the kind of place where zoning may be revisited as enrollment arrives.

## Location and commute

State Highway 46 on the west side of Boerne. You are close to town — the H-E-B, downtown, and Boerne High School are all short drives. I-10 access is a bit further than from the south-side neighborhoods, so the San Antonio commute is moderate.

## Amenities

None confirmed. At this stage of development, ask the builder what is committed in writing and what the HOA budget funds.

## Who it suits

name: Sundance Ranch
metaTitle: Sundance Ranch, Boerne TX 78006 — Guide, HOA, School District
metaDescription: Sundance Ranch, Boerne 78006: 162 homes off Toutant Beauregard in BEXAR County and NORTHSIDE ISD, not Boerne ISD. HOA fees, values, and honest fit.
body:
Sundance Ranch is a half-acre-lot community off Toutant Beauregard Road near Scenic Loop, west of I-10 and southwest of Boerne. The street names are a geologist's and a botanist's list combined — Buffalo Clover, Campo Viejo, Clyde Rock, Colts Foot, Desert Rainbow, Eufaula, Hutton Stone, Purple Hackett, Pyrite, Spider Rock, Star Mica, Wild Sage.

It sits immediately next to Anaqua Springs Ranch, and it shares that community's two most important facts.

## The school district — NOT Boerne ISD

**Sundance Ranch is in Northside ISD.**

We verified this two independent ways:

1. **Bexar County's own school district GIS layer** returns **Northside ISD** for this location.
2. **Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder address lookup returns no assignment.** We probed **nine parcels** spread across the community — Purple Hackett, Buffalo Clover, Star Mica, Wild Sage, Desert Rainbow, Clyde Rock. **All nine came back outside Boerne ISD.**

The address says Boerne, Texas 78006 — the same zip code as downtown Boerne. **The schools are Northside ISD.**

If you are moving to the area for Boerne ISD, Sundance Ranch does not deliver it. Verify the specific campus assignment with Northside ISD directly; we are not naming campuses we have not confirmed for this address.

## The county

**Sundance Ranch is in Bexar County.** The association's filed management certificate records the subdivision plats in the **Official Deed and Plat Records of Bexar County, Texas** (Bexar County Document No. 20220034746, filed February 10, 2022), and Bexar County's parcel records carry all 162 parcels.

Not the City of Boerne. Not Kendall County. Bexar County tax rates, Bexar County services.

We could not confirm whether the community is in unincorporated Bexar County or inside a city's extraterritorial jurisdiction.

## The numbers

Bexar County parcel records show **162 parcels**, with a **median lot of about 0.54 acres** and a **median total appraised value near $770,000**. Construction runs **2007 through 2024, with a median year built of 2011** (Bexar County parcel GIS, retrieved September 2026).

Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

The half-acre median lot is the distinguishing feature. That is roughly two and a half times the typical lot in Balcones Creek, Front Gate, Fallbrook or Sablechase, without moving into full acreage territory. For a buyer who wants meaningful separation from the neighbors but does not want to manage several acres, this is a useful middle ground — and there is not much else like it in the corridor.

## Development timeline

The association's certificate records the **Unit 1 Master Declaration executed October 19, 2007**, with **Unit 2 added in 2012** and **Unit 2A in 2021**. So the community platted in three stages over fourteen years, and construction has continued into 2024.

That means genuinely mixed vintages: some homes are approaching twenty years old, some are brand new. Pull the year built on the specific property; at this price point the difference between a 2008 house and a 2022 house is substantial.

## HOA — including a fee most communities do not have

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is the **Lot Owners' Association for Sundance Ranch, Inc.**, a Texas nonprofit corporation managed by **Diamond Association Management and Consulting** of San Antonio.

The filed certificate discloses an unusual and useful level of detail:

- **Transfer fee: $175**
- **Trash service: $73.20 per quarter**, billed together with assessments
- **Builder origination fee: $285**

That quarterly trash charge is worth noting. In unincorporated county areas there is no municipal trash service, so the association contracts it and bills owners — roughly **$293 per year on top of whatever the base assessment is.** Buyers coming from a city, where trash is bundled into the utility bill, routinely miss this.

**The base recurring assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate. Get it from Diamond Association Management, and make sure you understand whether the trash charge is included in or additional to it.

## Utilities

Not confirmed from a primary source. Look at the immediate neighbor for a clue: **Anaqua Springs Ranch, directly adjacent, has SAWS municipal water and private homeowner-maintained septic.** A similar arrangement at Sundance Ranch would be unsurprising, but **that is an inference, not a verified fact.**

Confirm the water provider and the wastewater arrangement in writing. If it is septic on a half-acre lot, pay close attention to the drainfield size, the system type, the permit, and whether there is room for a replacement field. Half an acre is workable for septic but it is not generous.

## Amenities and gating

We could not confirm an amenity package or gating status from a primary source. Verify on the ground.

## Location and commute

Off Toutant Beauregard Road near Scenic Loop, west of I-10. You are in the far northwest Bexar County corridor — closer to the I-10 and Loop 1604 retail and medical than to downtown Boerne, which is a real drive from here.

The Scenic Loop and Toutant Beauregard corridor is winding two-lane road in places. It is a pleasant drive and not a fast one.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants a half-acre lot, a quiet wooded corridor, and reasonable access to northwest San Antonio, and for whom Northside ISD is fine or preferred. It suits people who want more land than a tract subdivision without taking on acreage.

It does not suit a family relocating for Boerne ISD schools — this is Northside ISD. It does not suit someone who wants to live in the town of Boerne. And it does not suit a buyer who budgets HOA dues without adding the quarterly trash charge and, most likely, septic maintenance.

name: Tapatio Springs
metaTitle: Tapatio Springs, Boerne TX — Neighborhood Guide, HOA, Golf, Schools
metaDescription: Tapatio Springs in Boerne: 415 parcels, unincorporated Kendall County. Resort vs. HOA, golf membership costs, condos vs. single-family, schools.
body:
Tapatio Springs sits west of town off Johns Road, far enough out that the hills close in around it. It is a golf resort with houses attached, not a subdivision with a golf course bolted on, and that ordering matters for everything from what you pay monthly to what your neighbor's house is doing when you are not there.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **415 parcels in Tapatio Springs across roughly 435 acres**, with **284 carrying an improvement** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). That leaves a meaningful share still unbuilt.

Lot sizes are unusually spread out for a single community: 10th percentile about **0.19 acres**, median **0.43 acres**, 90th percentile about **1.17 acres**. That spread is the tell — Tapatio Springs is really several products in one place. There are condominium and townhome sections, garden-home sections, and full single-family lots on an acre or more.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels run a **median near $722,000**, with the 10th percentile around $443,000 and the 90th around $998,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

Streets like Blue Heron, Cliffdwellers, Antelope Hill, Arboleda, Axis and Cottontail carry a mix of eras. Some of the condominium stock dates to the resort's earlier decades and reads that way — vaulted ceilings, lots of glass aimed at the course. Newer single-family sections are Hill Country traditional. A number of units here have historically been used as second homes and short-stay rentals because of the resort, so occupancy patterns on some streets are different from a typical neighborhood. If full-time-neighbors matters to you, ask about it specifically for the section you are considering.

## HOA — and the fact that there is more than one

This is where Tapatio Springs gets genuinely complicated, and where most published information about it is wrong by oversimplification.

There is no single Tapatio Springs association. Texas HOA management certificate filings show **at least six distinct associations** tied to the community, all separately registered:

- Tapatio Springs Homeowners Association, Inc.
- The Ridge at Tapatio Springs Owners Association, Inc.
- The Gardens Over Tapatio Springs Owners Association
- Highlands at Tapatio Springs Homeowners Association, Inc.
- Heartland at Tapatio Springs Property Owners Association
- The Ridgeview Condominiums at Tapatio Springs Owners Association (a condominium association, not a POA)

Which one governs your property depends entirely on which section you buy in, and the dues differ enormously between them. Condominium and townhome sections carry exterior maintenance and therefore much higher monthly assessments than a single-family lot does. Any blanket statement about "the Tapatio Springs HOA fee" is meaningless — the correct question is always *which association, and what does it cover*.

The main Tapatio Springs Homeowners Association, Inc. is managed by Alamo Association Management Group out of San Antonio, and its filed certificate discloses a **$250 transfer fee** (recorded Kendall County Instrument #390661, filed July 19, 2024). Note that the management company's San Antonio address is where the manager sits — it says nothing about where the property is.

## The resort and golf club are separate money

The golf course, clubhouse, and resort operate commercially. They are not the residential HOA, and owning here does not make you a member. Golf memberships have their own initiation fees and monthly dues in tiers. Some home purchases have historically been marketed with an introductory membership attached; that is a deal term to get in writing, not a standing feature.

The practical upshot: you can own a home at Tapatio Springs and pay nothing to the golf club, or you can be a club member without living here. Two separate decisions, two separate budgets.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026). Confirm your specific address with the district — Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in 2024 and warns that addresses near boundary lines need verification.

## Jurisdiction and location

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Tapatio Springs parcels — this is **unincorporated Kendall County**, not inside the City of Boerne.

The drive matters here. Tapatio Springs is genuinely west of Boerne, out Johns Road. Getting to the H-E-B, to I-10, or to the high school is a real drive on two-lane road, and in the dark it is a deer-heavy one. People who love it here consider that a feature. People who need to be somewhere at 7:40 a.m. every morning should drive the route at that hour before they commit.

## Utilities

Utility service has not been independently verified for each section and is not disclosed on the management certificates. Given the resort infrastructure, some sections are on central systems — but do not assume it, and do not assume the condominium sections and the outlying single-family lots are on the same arrangement. Confirm water and wastewater in writing for the specific property.

## Who it suits

It suits a golfer who will actually play the course, a lock-and-leave buyer who wants a low-maintenance condominium in a scenic setting, or a second-home buyer who wants Hill Country without building. It suits someone who values the setting over proximity.

It does not suit a buyer who wants to be close in to Boerne, who needs a consistent HOA structure they can understand in one phone call, or who assumes a golf-course address includes golf. It also does not suit someone who wants a uniform, fully owner-occupied street — the mix here is genuinely mixed.

metaDescription: The Ranches at Creekside, Boerne: 532 homes on 306 platted acres inside City of Boerne limits. HOA fees, builders, schools, and honest fit.
body:
Despite the name, The Ranches at Creekside is not a ranch community. It is a conventional suburban subdivision on the east side of Boerne off Ammann Road, and it is one of the larger active new-construction neighborhoods in the city limits. Every street is named for a creek — Barton Creek, Beech Creek, Boulder Creek, Capano Creek, Carrizo Creek, Cimarron Creek, Cinnamon Creek, Coldwater Creek — which makes navigating it by address a small exercise in concentration.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **532 parcels across roughly 169 platted acres**, with **428 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). About 80% built out, so there is still active construction.

The association's own filed management certificate describes the underlying land as a tract of **approximately 306.76 acres** conveyed by special warranty deed and recorded in Kendall County. The difference between that figure and the 169 platted acres on the appraisal roll is the part not yet platted into lots — so more phases are coming.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.164 acres**, median **0.209 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.335 acres**. Builders market these around 65-foot widths.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $599,000**, 10th percentile around $513,000, 90th around $716,000. Appraisal-district values, not list prices.

## Housing stock

Production new construction. Highland Homes and Perry Homes have both been active here with their standard Texas plan libraries — one and two-story, three to five bedrooms, studies and game rooms, stone-and-stucco elevations. This is a predictable, warrantied product with design center options, not custom work.

Sections built at different times look different. Walk the older streets and the newest ones before you choose.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on all 532 parcels. Inside the city limits: city water and sewer, city trash, Boerne PD, city tax line. No well, no septic, and — importantly — **no utility district levy**, which distinguishes it from Esperanza across town.

If you are comparing The Ranches at Creekside against Esperanza on payment, that difference in tax structure is the thing to model. Do not compare list prices alone.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Ranches at Creekside Property Owners Association**, managed by FirstService Residential San Antonio (TREC management certificate, plats recorded Kendall County; Unit 4B plat Document No. 2020-349856).

The filed certificate discloses closing costs clearly: a **$375 resale certificate fee**, a **$340 transfer fee**, a **$150 refinance fee**, and a **$500 working capital fee**.

**The recurring annual assessment is not disclosed** on the certificate. Get it from FirstService Residential before your option period ends.

## Amenities

Walking and biking trails and green space are in place. Secondary sources describe a **developer-planned amenity center that was not yet built** as of their publication.

If an amenity center factors into your decision, get it in writing from the developer: what is planned, what is funded, and what the delivery date is. Planned amenities at partially built subdivisions slip regularly, and a rendering in a sales office is not a commitment. Ask whether the HOA budget currently includes operating costs for it — that tells you whether it is real.

We found no source confirming the community is gated, and its location inside city limits suggests public streets.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Cibolo Creek Elementary, Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address. Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries when Viola Wilson Elementary opened in August 2024, and a subdivision still adding phases is exactly the kind of place where future boundaries may shift.

## Location and commute

East Boerne off Ammann Road, reached from Highway 46 East. You are close to the Highway 46 retail corridor, a short run to downtown Boerne, and a reasonable drive to I-10. Champion High School is nearby, which matters if you have teenagers driving themselves.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants new construction with a builder warranty, city utilities without a utility district tax, and a straightforward Boerne address at a mid-market price. It suits families who want to be on the Champion side of town.

It does not suit anyone who wants acreage, trees, or privacy — the name notwithstanding, lots are about a fifth of an acre. name: The Woods of Boerne
metaTitle: The Woods of Boerne, TX — Neighborhood Guide, HOA, Schools
metaDescription: The Woods of Boerne: 202 homes on wooded lots inside city limits, across Hwy 46 from Champion High. HOA fees, schools, and an honest fit assessment.
body:
The Woods of Boerne is a small, tucked-in neighborhood on Highway 46 East, essentially across the road from Champion High School. The name is accurate — this is one of the better-canopied newer subdivisions in town, and the street names lean into it: Alder Woods, Arbor Woods, Enchanted Woods, Massey Woods, Noble Woods, Woods Crossing.

It is easy to drive past. Entrances off a state highway rarely announce themselves, and this one does not.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **202 parcels across roughly 68 acres**, with **188 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). At 93% built out with only 68 total acres, this is a compact, essentially finished neighborhood. There is no future phase coming.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.165 acres**, median **0.193 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.377 acres**. Call it a fifth of an acre typical, with a handful of larger lots at the edges.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $536,000**, 10th percentile around $435,000, 90th around $685,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

Single-family homes, mostly two-story, in the 2,300 to 4,100 square foot range depending on plan. Three-car garages are common. Elevations run stone-and-stucco with some board-and-batten accents. This was production-built to a move-up buyer, not a starter buyer — floor plans tend to include a study, a game room, and a formal dining room.

The lots being wooded is a real differentiator in this price band. Most subdivisions in Boerne at this price were scraped flat and replanted. Several streets here kept mature oaks, and it changes how the neighborhood feels in August.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on all 202 parcels. This is inside the city limits: city utilities, city police, city trash, and a city tax line. On a fifth-acre lot that is what you want — you are not dealing with a septic system or a well.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Woods of Boerne Homeowners Association, Inc.**, managed by Alamo Management Company out of San Antonio (amended and restated TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County Instrument #403047, filed October 22, 2025).

The filed certificate discloses the closing-table charges clearly: a **$500 working capital assessment**, a **$250 resale transfer fee**, and a **$250 resale certificate fee**, with rush tiers up to $450 and a $75 update fee. Those are reasonable and in line with peers.

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the management certificate, and we could not verify it from a primary source. Texas only requires transfer-related fees on that filing. Get the current annual or quarterly assessment from Alamo Management directly before your option period ends.

The community is commonly described as gated. We were not able to confirm that from a primary source, and the fact that it sits inside city limits raises the question of whether the streets are public or private. Verify it on a drive-through — it takes thirty seconds and it affects both access and who maintains the pavement.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Dr. Ferdinand L. Herff Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

This is a genuinely counterintuitive result and worth pausing on: **The Woods of Boerne is directly across Highway 46 from Champion High School, but it is zoned to Boerne High School.** Proximity is not zoning. If you are buying here specifically because of a school, run your exact address through the district's lookup and confirm it in writing. Boerne ISD also redrew elementary boundaries when Viola Wilson Elementary opened in August 2024, so anything published before then is unreliable.

## Location and commute

Highway 46 East puts you a few minutes from the H-E-B and the main retail corridor, and a reasonable run to I-10 for the San Antonio commute. Downtown Boerne and the Hill Country Mile are close — a short drive, not walkable, but close enough to be routine.

Being on a state highway has the usual tradeoff. Access is excellent. Turning left out of the neighborhood at 5:15 p.m. is less excellent. Drive it at rush hour.

## Amenities

Modest. There is no pool or clubhouse that we could confirm. The selling points here are the trees, the lot sizes, the location, and the small scale — 202 homes is a neighborhood you can actually learn.

If a pool or an amenity center is a requirement for you, this is not the one; Regent Park, Esperanza, and Southglen all have more.

## Who it suits

It suits a move-up buyer who wants a larger house on a wooded lot inside Boerne city limits, with a short drive to shopping and a manageable commute. It suits someone who values mature trees and a finished, quiet neighborhood over an amenity package.

It does not suit a buyer who wants acreage or a view. It does not suit someone who wants a community pool, a gym, or an active social calendar. And it does not suit anyone assuming the high school across the street is the assigned high school — it is not.

body:
The Woods of Frederick Creek is a compact neighborhood on the west side of Boerne near Johns Road, close enough to downtown that it is one of the few modern subdivisions where walking to the Hill Country Mile is at least arguable. The street names lean hard into Boerne's German heritage — Bonn, Brunswick, Hagen, Kassel, Krieg, Kasper, Fischer, Benton, Chisholm — which is a nice touch in a part of town that earns it.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **214 parcels across roughly 67 acres**, with **207 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). At 97% built out on 67 acres, this is a small, finished neighborhood. Nothing more is coming.

Lots: 10th percentile about **0.14 acres**, median **0.17 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.28 acres**. Small, conventional suburban lots.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $458,000**, 10th percentile around $391,000, 90th around $540,000. That is a tight, accessible band — one of the more attainable neighborhoods in Boerne proper. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices.

## Housing stock

Production single-family homes, with Armadillo Homes identified as the builder in secondary sources. Development dates to roughly 2010. Expect one and two-story plans, conventional elevations, attached garages, and small yards.

Because the neighborhood built out over a relatively short window, the homes are consistent in age and condition — most are now in the 12-to-16-year range, which is the window where original roofs, water heaters, and first HVAC systems come due. Factor that into an offer.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on all 214 parcels. Inside the city limits: City of Boerne water, sewer, and electric service, city trash, Boerne PD. This is a real advantage on a sixth-acre lot and it is one of the main reasons this neighborhood makes sense at its price.

The filed certificate discloses a **$375 transfer fee** and a **$325 resale certificate assembly fee**.

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the certificate. One secondary source states $150 per quarter, but that is unverified and we are not going to present it as fact. Confirm with RealManage directly before your option period ends.

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the neighborhood returns **Fabra Elementary, Boerne Middle School North, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address with the district. Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in August 2024 when Viola Wilson Elementary opened, and this neighborhood sits close enough to the Fabra and Curington boundary that verification is worth the phone call.

## Location and commute

This is the neighborhood's best feature. You are on the west side of town near Johns Road, minutes from downtown Boerne, minutes from Boerne High School, and a straightforward run to I-10. For a buyer who wants to be genuinely *in* Boerne rather than on the edge of it, this is one of the better-positioned modern subdivisions in the city.

Downtown is close. Whether it is walkable depends on which street you are on and how you feel about walking a mile each way — call it bikeable and honest.

## Amenities

Minimal. We found no confirmed pool, clubhouse, or amenity center. The dues here are correspondingly modest, and the value proposition is location and price rather than facilities.

If you want a pool and a gym in the HOA, look at Regent Park or Esperanza instead — both cost more per month for the privilege.

It suits a buyer who wants to live close to downtown Boerne, inside the city limits, on full city utilities, at one of the lower price points available in town. It suits a first-time buyer, a downsizer, or someone who works in Boerne itself. It suits people who would rather spend their money on location than on amenities.

Trails of Herff Ranch is one of the most practical buys in Boerne, and that is the whole point of it. At 98% built out, this is a finished neighborhood — what you see is what it will be. That is worth something. You are not buying next to a future phase.

Lots are small and consistent: 10th percentile about **0.114 acres**, median **0.138 acres**, 90th percentile about **0.22 acres**. Roughly a sixth of an acre is the norm.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $388,000**, 10th percentile around $320,000, 90th around $480,000. That is the tightest and most affordable band of any established Kendall County neighborhood covered in this guide. These are appraisal-district values, not list prices.

## Housing stock

Production-built single-family homes, predominantly from the 2007-2017 window, in one- and two-story plans. Three to five bedrooms is the normal range. Elevations are stone-and-stucco or stone-and-siding, standard suburban massing. You will not find custom architecture here, and you will not pay for it either.

Because the community filled in over roughly a decade in eight platted units, the older sections have mature landscaping and the later ones do not. Walk both before you decide which part you want.

## Jurisdiction — inside the City of Boerne

Kendall CAD parcel records show the **City of Boerne** as a taxing unit on every parcel in Trails of Herff Ranch. This is genuinely **inside the city limits** — which means Boerne PD, City of Boerne utilities, city trash, and a city property tax line on your bill. That distinguishes it from the acreage communities out in unincorporated Kendall County, where you get a lower tax rate and no city services.

For most buyers looking in this price band, being inside the city is a feature, not a cost. City water and sewer beats a well and a septic field when you are on a sixth of an acre.

## HOA — and the transfer charge that catches people

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is the **Homeowners Association of Herff Ranch in Boerne, Inc.**, managed by RealManage (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County, filed November 30, 2021). Note the legal name differs from the marketing name — you will see the neighborhood called "Trails of Herff Ranch," "Trails at Herff Ranch," and just "Herff Ranch." They are the same place.

The filed certificate discloses the closing costs, and one of them is unusual enough to flag: a **$375 resale certificate fee**, a **$325 transfer fee**, and a **working capital charge of the greater of $100 or 15% of the sale price, due from the purchaser at closing.**

Read that again. Fifteen percent of the sale price as a working capital contribution would be an extraordinary figure — far outside the norm, where working capital charges are typically a few hundred dollars or a couple months' assessments. Either this provision is being applied differently in practice than it reads, or it is a drafting artifact in the filing. **Do not close on a home here without getting the actual working capital figure confirmed in writing by RealManage before your option period ends.** This is the most financially significant unverified item in this guide.

The recurring dues amount is not disclosed on the management certificate — Texas only requires transfer-related fees there. Get the current assessment from RealManage directly.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Cibolo Creek Elementary, Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School, and Champion High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Worth noting: this is a Champion High School neighborhood, not a Boerne High School one, despite being closer to the center of town than several Boerne High neighborhoods. Boerne ISD's boundaries do not follow intuition. Confirm your specific address with the district, especially given the 2024 elementary boundary redraw.

## Location and commute

This is the strongest argument for Trails of Herff Ranch. You are minutes from Highway 46, minutes from the H-E-B, and a short run to I-10. Downtown Boerne and the Hill Country Mile are close enough to be a normal Saturday rather than an expedition. Commuting into San Antonio is about as good as it gets from a Boerne address.

## Amenities

Community pool, playground, sport court, and green space with a connected trail network. Modest, maintained, and appropriate to the dues level.

One item to verify: sources disagree on whether the community is gated. Kendall CAD shows the neighborhood inside the City of Boerne, which usually implies city-maintained public streets rather than private gated ones. Confirm before relying on it either way.

## Who it suits

It suits a first-time or move-up buyer who wants a Boerne address, Boerne ISD schools, and city utilities without an acreage price tag. It suits someone who wants a finished neighborhood with no construction traffic. It suits a commuter.

It does not suit a buyer who wants land, privacy, or a view. On a sixth of an acre you will know your neighbors well. It does not suit someone looking for custom character or mature oaks. And it does not suit anyone who signs without first nailing down that working capital number.

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. body:
Waterstone is an acreage community northeast of Boerne with private river parks on the Guadalupe. The roads are named for Texas rivers — Concho, Llano, Nueces, Pecos, San Saba, Rio Brazos, Rio Colorado, Rio Frio — plus Guadalupe Bend, which is the one that tells you what people buy here for.

It sits off FM 3351, out past where the subdivisions stop and the ranch gates start.

## The numbers

Kendall County Appraisal District parcel records show **222 parcels covering roughly 1,266 acres**, with **181 already improved** (Kendall CAD GIS parcel layer, retrieved September 2026). About 82% built out, so there is still some vacant land trading.

These are real acreage lots: 10th percentile about **3.17 acres**, median **4.84 acres**, 90th percentile about **8.75 acres**. Five acres is the normal Waterstone lot.

Current Kendall CAD market values on improved parcels: **median near $961,000**, 10th percentile around $739,000, 90th around $1,294,000. Appraisal-district values, not asking prices. Compared to Cordillera Ranch or Sabinas Creek Ranch, Waterstone is the more affordable way into gated acreage with river access — that is its market position and it is a fair one.

## Housing stock

Custom homes on acreage, built across roughly the last two decades. There is no single architectural signature; you will see Hill Country limestone, some Texas farmhouse, and some fairly conventional stucco. Square footages vary widely because each was built for its owner.

Because lots are five acres, homes are far apart and largely invisible from the road. Expect long driveways, propane tanks, and detached shops. Horses are common in this part of the county.

## The river — what you are actually buying

The community's amenity is **two private riverfront parks on the Guadalupe**, with a pavilion, picnic tables, and grills, for swimming, fishing, and kayaking. Individual lots are generally not on the river; the river access is a shared, gated amenity.

That distinction is the one to get right. "Waterstone on the Guadalupe" does not mean your lot fronts the Guadalupe. A very small number of parcels may; most do not. If river frontage on your own deed matters to you, verify it on the survey — do not infer it from the subdivision name.

## HOA

**The HOA is mandatory.** The association is **Waterstone on the Guadalupe Property Owners Association**, a Texas nonprofit corporation, managed by Diamond Association Management and Consulting out of San Antonio (TREC management certificate, recorded Kendall County Instrument #361120, filed September 7, 2021).

The filed certificate discloses a **$175 property transfer fee** — notably modest compared to peers like Cordillera Ranch ($2,000 working capital) or Sabinas Creek Ranch ($340 transfer plus a $375 resale certificate).

**The recurring dues amount is not disclosed** on the certificate. One secondary source puts annual dues around $715, but we could not confirm that from the association, and secondary dues figures for Boerne neighborhoods are wrong often enough that you should not rely on it. Get the current assessment from Diamond Association Management directly.

## Jurisdiction and taxes

Kendall CAD shows **no city taxing unit** on Waterstone parcels. This is **unincorporated Kendall County** — no city property tax, no city services. Sheriff, not city police. County permitting. Rural fire response.

## Utilities — assume well and septic until told otherwise

We were not able to verify water and wastewater service for Waterstone from a primary source. Given five-acre lots this far out on FM 3351, individual wells and on-site septic systems are the overwhelmingly likely arrangement, but **that is an inference, not a confirmed fact.** Confirm it in writing for the specific property, and if it is a well, get the well log, the depth, the pump age, and a water quality test. On acreage in Kendall County that inspection line item is not optional.

## Schools

**Boerne ISD.** A point inside the community returns **Dr. Ferdinand L. Herff Elementary, Capt. Mark Tyler Voss Middle School, and Boerne High School** through Boerne ISD's own InfoFinder lookup (queried September 2026).

Confirm your specific address. Waterstone is spread over 1,266 acres, Boerne ISD redrew elementary boundaries in August 2024, and the district explicitly asks that addresses near boundary lines be verified with Administrative Services.

Be realistic about the bus. On five-acre lots this far from town, the school run is a real part of your day.

## Location and commute

This is the honest part. Waterstone is northeast of Boerne on FM 3351, and it is not close to anything. Getting to the H-E-B is a drive. Getting to Boerne High School is a drive. Getting to I-10 and then into San Antonio is a commute you will feel every single day.

People who live here have made peace with that, and in exchange they get five acres, oak trees, quiet, and a private stretch of the Guadalupe. It is a genuinely good trade for the right household. It is a miserable one for the wrong household, and the wrong household usually figures that out about eight months in.

Drive the route to your actual workplace, at your actual departure time, before you write an offer.

## Who it suits

It suits a buyer who wants acreage and real river access without Cordillera Ranch pricing, who works from home or has a tolerant commute, and who is comfortable with a well, a septic system, and county services. It suits people with horses, boats, and kayaks.

It does not suit a commuter with a hard 8:00 a.m. start in San Antonio, a family that wants to walk to things, or a buyer who has never owned on a well and does not want to learn. It also does not suit anyone expecting their own river frontage — check the survey.

## Talk to someone who works this market

Heath Shepard is a licensed Texas REALTOR with Keller Williams, working Boerne, Fair Oaks Ranch, and Kendall County. If you want current Waterstone listings, or help sorting out which lots actually touch the river and what the well and septic situation is, reach out through theheathshepardrealestateteam.com.
